cdb8d3c66fa99474: The latest interim release of Ubuntu is here, complete with kernel 7.3 – even though it isn't officially out yet. It also includes a new speech-to-text system that is intriguing but not fully useful. Ubuntu 26.10 "Stonking Stingray" arrived on time. This is just a couple of weeks after the beta version that we looked at earlier this month, suggesting that the team didn’t encounter any show-stopper bugs. The faster kernel release cycle that Canonical adopted in 2024 has slightly bitten them this time around: the Linux kernel’s new faster AI-boosted release cycle means that 7.2 is relatively old now, but 7.3 isn’t quite ready yet; at the time of writing, it’s on Release Candidate 7 – but Canonical has jumped the gun and used it anyway. So, the release version of Ubuntu 26.10 comes with a pre-release kernel, and machines will get updated to the completed 7.3 as soon as it’s available. We tried the default GNOME edition, with GNOME 51. It looks identical to the beta version. The most visible difference in this release is in the window-tiling assistant, which now displays a Windows-like transient pop-up box offering various tiled arrangements when you drag a window to the edge of the screen. The Myna speech-to-text tool, whose announcement we covered back in June, is now available – albeit as a technology preview. We tested the beta on an old ThinkPad, and while the pre-release OS ran perfectly, Myna didn't work. (Incidentally, after switching to a non-GPU LLM, it does work in the release version – just very slowly.) So, we tried the release version on our newer testbed machine, a Dell XPS 9370. The installation process is more straightforward now, with some official instructions, and as the Dell doesn't have an unsupported Nvidia GPU to complicate things, it worked fine. The installation pulls in nearly a gigabyte of dependencies and language model files: since the installation ISO is already 6⅔ GB, it's probably a good thing that it’s not included. We tested it in the Writer module of LibreOffice 26.8. Invoking it is as simple as pressing Super+J, and then talking. Using the laptop’s built-in microphone, accuracy was poor, but with a USB headset, it improved markedly. It’s a little odd to watch as the model revises the text as you go along, going back and altering words as later ones resolve ambiguities, but it did the job. It doesn’t understand punctuation or commands: words such as "comma," "full stop," "new line," "delete," and so on, were entered into the document along with other text. For a preview, though, it's impressive, and for those who have problems with the use of their arms – such as the Reg FOSS desk just three years ago – this is a seriously useful extra. Ubuntu now just has to catch up with macOS and Windows, both of which have offered speech input for several years – but it's finally entered the race. This is one use of LLMs of which we heartily approve. Alongside the flagship GNOME edition, all the flavors have been updated, which hasn't happened for about a year. For some flavors, this means new versions of their respective desktops, depending on the release cycle of the respective environment. As we said when we looked at the beta release, Kubuntu 26.10 comes with KDE Plasma 6.7.5, which is the final Plasma release to support X11. Although Ubuntu MATE skipped the LTS release earlier this year, it's back with the Stonking release: Ubuntu MATE 26.10 will come as good news for fans of this retro GNOME 2 style desktop. A year ago, Ubuntu Unity missed the 25.10 release, and 26.04 is not an LTS, so fans of Canonical's in-house desktop should take a close look at Ubuntu Unity 26.10. A visible change from previous releases is that it's picked up some accessory apps from the Lomiri desktop, which is the community continuation of what was going to be Unity 8. Ubuntu Unity 26.10 uses the Lomiri terminal emulator by default, and Lomiri's File Manager is available as an alternative to the default Nemo file manager. The "minimal" installation of this release is even more stripped back than Xubuntu Minimal – this version doesn't have the Snap subsystem installed at all. Ubuntu Budgie 26.10 has the very latest Budgie desktop version 10.10.3, which brings some accessibility improvements. Ubuntu Cinnamon 26.10 has an updated version of Mint’s Cinnamon environment, too – it includes the very latest Cinnamon 6.6.9, released in June. Lubuntu 26.10 includes the latest LXQt 2.4, which arrived too close to the release of Lubuntu 26.04 to be incorporated. The other 26.10 flavors are more modest releases, which just pick up the latest versions of their components. Under the hood, there are some deeper changes that affect all editions. As we mentioned in the beta version, more core CLI tools have been replaced with new Rust versions, now including the NTP-sync daemon. Stonking replaces dbus-daemon with dbus-broker, and it uses systemd 261.3. The server version has been updated as well, and now includes AMD ROCm 10.0, OpenSSL 4, OpenSSH 10.5, and the Rust upki tool for revoking security certificates. Canonical’s home-grown TPM-backed full disk encryption is present, but intrepid experimenters who have enabled that on 26.04 can't upgrade for now – this should follow later. One of the benefits of increasingly mature FOSS desktops is that upgrades are increasingly routine, so long as you haven't rolled up your sleeves, lifted the hood, and started customizing the OS. If you just install packages from Snapcraft and leave the OS alone, interim versions are pretty safe these days, and so is the upgrade process. It's one way to avoid being nagged about Ubuntu Pro, if that irks you. Pro is not available on interim releases. By default, LTS versions don't automatically offer to upgrade to interim ones – if you want it, you must opt in. We suggest leaving it until the final version of the kernel, but otherwise, it’s already in good shape. ®

b11861f5bb0a456c: For lawyers who love to use AI to write legal briefs, there's just one problem: bots hallucinate and make things up. Fortunately, a new tool, CiteProof, promises to crawl over briefs and filings for fabricated case citations and misquoted court opinions before they result in sanctions, fines, or just plain embarrassing dressing downs from a judge. This is hardly a new problem, with lawyers relying on AI to do their work for several years with predictably horrible results. Even if GPT-4 was capable of passing a bar exam in 2023, that doesn’t mean it wasn’t hallucinating case law. OpenAI models aren’t alone in getting lawyers in trouble, either - Claude was actually thrown under the bus by Anthropic’s own lawyers last year when defending the company from a music publishing copyright lawsuit. A declaration in the case from an Anthropic data scientist contained a pair of Claude-formatted citations that pointed to improper records, and lawyers didn’t catch it in review. The lawyers blamed Claude for the issue. Stories of AI hallucinations winding up in legal briefs are everywhere nowadays, and have had serious consequences beyond professional rebukes: A Georgia court decision was even vacated last year after a court order was found to contain fictional citations. In short, AI and the legal world, which demands precision and accuracy, don’t always mix, so a fact checker that can do a better job than apparently absent-minded human reviewers is needed. CiteProof wants to be that fact checker. Free users can run individual checks through CiteProof to look for citations or statutes, while paid users can run in-depth scans that include more detailed verification reports, quotation checking, bulk scanning, and the like. CiteProof admitted that, as a small operation, some vibe-coding was involved in the creation of the platform, but no AI is involved in checking legal briefs for AI. “You cannot reliably catch AI hallucinations with more AI guesswork,” a CiteProof spokesperson told us. “This is the foundational principle of CiteProof.” There aren’t any LLMs or probabilistic models under CiteProof’s hood, we’re told, with queries instead relying on direct, deterministic searches of public court records to look for evidence that what AI is citing for lawyers isn’t being completely made up. It’s not going to tell you whether you’re making a good argument, mind you - CiteProof is just going to free up that legal assistant to do something more productive than checking citations. The only thing that leaves CiteProof’s servers, the company claims, is strings extracted from citations that can be input into CourtListener to figure out if they’re real. Everything runs in the US, and nothing is stored or transmitted to an LLM at any point, CiteProof says. But why encourage lawyers to use more AI if it’s not a reliable tool for their purposes? The genie is already out of the bottle, CiteProof says, even if it is a real messy genie who just makes stuff up. “Lawyers and associates are already using AI to speed up research and drafting, and that adoption isn't stopping,” the representative told us. “CiteProof isn't encouraging blind AI adoption—it acts as an objective, non-AI guardrail to ensure that if someone uses generative tools to draft, fabricated citations are caught before hitting a court docket.” It’s better than nothing, even if it doesn’t come cheap: A single brief costs $49 to check if you don’t opt for the limited free tier, with bundles offering multiple briefs at a discount ($199 for a five-pack), all the way up to $499 a month for 200 brief reviews for law firms that just can’t stop relying on AI to make their arguments for them. ®

68b02ba462b0e816: Kendall Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is often cited as the most innovative square mile in the world. But when the Kendall Square Association gathered local stakeholders for its 18th Annual Meeting Thursday, the conversation focused on innovation primarily in the context of community. The event, which took place at the nonprofit startup incubator The Engine, attracted people from across Cambridge, including business leaders, elected officials, local residents, and students, for a night of local food and conversation about the advance of technologies like artificial intelligence and what they mean for society. “How can we make AI not an enemy of work, but a tool for workers to expand their capabilities and build new expertise or do new things?” asked MIT Institute Professor Daron Acemoglu in a keynote talk. “The world is at a point in time where we need new innovations and new adaptations to growing challenges.” Acemoglu’s keynote was one of several presentations at the event, which also featured music from the Kendall Square Orchestra, a vote on new KSA board members, and awards for organizations making a positive impact through innovation. KSA is a nonprofit made up of over 150 organizations across Kendall Square, from major companies to universities, research organizations, and the independent shops and restaurants that give Kendall Square its distinct character. “People come to Kendall Square to make the world better,” said KSA Executive Director Beth O’Neill Maloney in her opening remarks. “People come here to improve the human condition, people come here to solve big problems, and people come here to innovate for good.” Acemoglu, who shared the Nobel Prize in economics in 2024 for his work studying how institutions affect prosperity, spoke on the subject of his new book, “What Happened to Liberal Democracy?” Acemoglu says liberal democracy is under siege as trust in liberal institutions decline, political polarization rises, and people lose faith in elected officials. He acknowledged that the shared prosperity liberal democracy promised has not always been delivered, especially over the last 50 years, but insisted it is the best path forward and in need of renewed support. “I believe liberal democratic institutions, together with the norms that support them, are one of the greatest human achievements,” Acemoglu said. “It would be unthinkable for people who lived 300 years ago that we could live in societies consisting of hundreds of millions of people with diverse interests, different views, doing different things, and people still participate in politics and reach compromises, and we have state institutions that, by and large, actually provide services and do things for the people, and that we build opportunities for prosperity from which most people benefit while social freedoms are largely upheld.” Cambridge Mayor Sumbul Siddiqui also spoke at the event. Siddiqui began her talk by telling the story of Cambridge residents working with biotech labs in the 1970s to create a groundbreaking policy on recombinant DNA research, which helped turn Kendall Square into the life science hub it is today. “All these years later I think that story captures what makes Kendall Square so special: It’s our willingness to work together even when we face big challenges,” Siddiqui said. “It isn’t just the universities or labs, it’s also the culture of collaboration among nonprofits, governments, and residents.” Broad Institute Chief Communications Officer Lee McGuire started his talk by reviewing a 2009 report on what made Kendall Square such a powerful driver of innovation, noting that factors like talent density, education, and a collective voice remain strong in the area today. “This report was brilliant in that it captures so many of the special things that matter for a place like Kendall,” McGuire said. “It is the job of the Kendall Square Association and all of us to help protect those things, make sure we name them, understand them, and see them as essential elements of making sure this community stays what it is no matter what happens. As long as there’s a good idea, this is the place that’s going to get that idea moving and scale it up to change the world.”
896926e5635f588d: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has allocated a record RM57 billion in financing facilities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) under the 2027 Budget to help the sector navigate global economic uncertainties.

Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim said the allocation, up from RM50 billion previously, reflected the government's commitment to strengthening the sector through better access to financing, lower business costs and improved government service delivery.
He said the government understood the pressures MSMEs faced amid global economic fluctuations, including rising energy costs and supply chain disruptions beyond the country's control.
"We know that in a time of multiple crises, SMEs must be given breathing space so they can face the various challenges.

"We cannot control energy prices. We cannot control some of the supply chain. At least we can control the ground force here in Malaysia," he said at the Enterprise 50 (E50) Awards ceremony here tonight.
Also present was SME Corp Malaysia chief executive officer Rizal Nainy.
Sim also addressed the latest minimum wage increase, saying MSMEs had been granted an exemption to help ease their operating cost pressures.
However, he stressed that easing the burden on employers did not mean the government was abandoning its goal of creating high-income jobs for Malaysians.
"We all want to see Malaysians secure high-paying jobs, but as the world faces various crises, MSMEs also need to be given space to overcome these challenges," he said.

Sim said MSME performance was a key determinant of the nation's economic growth and expressed optimism that 2027 would be a better year for the sector, supported by government initiatives and the resilience of local entrepreneurs.
Meanwhile, Rizal said the E50 Business Matching programme organised by SME Corp Malaysia had generated RM420 million in potential sales.
He said the two-day programme, held in conjunction with the awards, aimed to expand MSMEs' access to export markets and create new business collaboration opportunities.
"This year's E50 programme took a more meaningful approach. It was expanded with the E50 Export Conference and the E50 Business Matching programme," he said.
Rizal added that the awards received 160 nominations this year, the highest number since their inception in 1997.
He said the increased participation reflected growing recognition of E50 as a platform showcasing the achievements of high-performing Malaysian MSMEs.
At the event, 50 MSMEs received the E50 Award in recognition of their achievements, performance and ability to expand their businesses.
The award recognises excellence in business growth, competitiveness, innovation and governance.
d0537ac761f5a595: WASHINGTON: Donald Trump did not request a reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine, a US official said Friday, after tech billionaire Elon Musk insisted any limits on the communications system would ultimately have come from the president.

Kyiv on Wednesday reported restrictions to the SpaceX-operated service, which it sees as crucial to fending off Moscow's invasion, shortly after Trump criticised Ukraine and urged it to stop targeting Russian oil refineries.
"No such request was ever made by the president," the US official said on condition of anonymity, when asked whether the order had come from the White House as reported by the Reuters news agency.
Musk has said that "any limits on speed or usage" of his SpaceX company's Starshield systems were "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," referring to Trump.
Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink's military-grade satellite service, for its battlefield communications, its mid-range strikes on Russia-occupied territory, and its interceptor drones.
It also uses SpaceX's parallel Starlink civilian satellite system.

Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky said Friday that the service was in the process of being restored, and that "my partners told me that the administration and the White House sent a message to SpaceX asking them" to do so.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have been increasingly tense in recent days, with Trump calling for Zelensky to be replaced after the Ukrainian leader slammed a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets.
70617b3878738701: PETALING JAYA: Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Ismail Lasim patut meletak jawatan selepas beliau ditegur secara terbuka oleh pemerintah negeri hari ini, menurut seorang peguam.

Rosli Dahlan berkata, teguran oleh Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir mendedahkan Ismail sebagai seorang 'pengkhianat', dan pengkhianatan ialah dosa besar dalam Islam, salah satu sifat munafik yang tidak melayakkan seseorang memegang jawatan awam.
"Letak jawatan dan bertaubat – paling tidak, ini yang Ismail boleh lakukan untuk menebus maruahnya," kata Rosli kepada FMT.

Rosli mendakwa Ismail 'tanpa segan silu' mengangkat sumpah jawatan menteri besar di hadapan Tuanku Muhriz pada 2 Ogos, kemudian menandatangani proklamasi yang dibuat beberapa bulan sebelumnya untuk melucutkan Tuanku Muhriz daripada takhta.

Beliau berkata, Ismail juga membuat laporan polis mendakwa bahawa dokumen itu telah beliau tandatangani secara paksaan dan mengesahkan proklamasi tersebut sebagai tidak sah. Beliau bagaimanapun mendorong ahli Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (exco) mengeluarkan kenyataan mengatakan proklamasi 'tidak sah' itu telah berkuat kuasa sejak 19 April.

"Sikap bolak-balik itu sepatutnya mengundang tindakan menurut undang-undang jenayah. Beliau patut dituduh kerana menyatakan maklumat palsu dan membuat laporan polis palsu. Beliau telah menipu secara terbuka namun tiada tindakan diambil terhadapnya," kata Rosli menambah, pada zaman dahulu, Ismail akan dihukum mati atas pengkhianatannya.
Rakaman memaparkan Tuanku Muhriz menempelak Ismail dimuat naik di media sosial petang tadi, memaparkan Tuanku Muhriz mempersoalkan tujuan Ismail berhasrat menemui baginda.

"Jadi (hari ini) dia nak datang jumpa saya buat apa? Selagi dia tidak tarik balik apa yang dikatakannya sebelum ini, jangan datang jumpa saya. Go away,” titah Tuanku Muhriz yang jelas kelihatan murka, sebelum berpaling ke arah Ismail.
Sebagai respons, Ismail hanya mampu mengangkat sembah.

Teguran Tuanku Muhriz terhadap Ismail berlatarkan krisis perlembagaan di Negeri Sembilan, tercetus apabila empat individu yang mendakwa diri mereka sebagai undang mengumumkan Tuanku Muhriz dilucutkan takhta selaku pemerintah negeri.
Kumpulan undang yang dipertikaikan itu turut didakwa mengisytiharkan Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar yang 'baharu'.
Bulan lepas, Ismail menyokong kenyataan yang dikeluarkan oleh barisan exconya yang kononnya mengesahkan penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Tuanku Muhriz kemudiannya membatalkan pelantikan keseluruhan barisan exco tersebut.
9f15671bcc3c7114: BAGHDAD: Iraq has lost around US$60 billion during the Middle East war, foreign minister Fuad Hussein said on Thursday, with Iran blockading a waterway that is crucial to global energy flows.
Opec member Iraq was producing about four million barrels of oil per day before the conflict, exporting about 3.5 million bpd - mostly shipped from the country's south via the Strait of Hormuz.
However, Iran's stranglehold on the waterway forced Iraq, lacking storage capacity, to halt most production and fall back on limited exports via Syria and Turkey, by truck and pipeline respectively.

"Iraq has suffered losses estimated at around 60 billion dollars during the recent war between the US and the Islamic Republic of Iran," Hussein told his Italian counterpart in Rome, according to a statement from the Iraqi foreign ministry.

After a heavy drop in production, Iraqi oil exports, which provide about 90% of the country's revenues, recovered modestly last month, reaching 2.6 million barrels per day between September 1 and 21, according to the oil ministry.
However, at the same time, Iraq's foreign currency reserves have shrunk by 20 billion dollars and consumer prices have risen sharply, plunging it into economic crisis.
To try to contain the fallout, the Central Bank of Iraq last week devalued the dinar against the dollar for the first time in more than three years.
Iraq relies heavily on foreign currency generated by oil sales to finance imports, stabilise the dinar, and pay the salaries of public sector employees and retirees.
According to the authorities, Iraq is seeking to diversify its economic resources and raise non-oil revenues from 10% to 45% by 2037.
ed60d0824b30682c: KUALA LUMPUR: Azfar Fikri Azhar shone with a brilliant hat-trick to steer Star City to a 5-2 victory over Kelantan Red Warrior (KRW) in their Super League encounter at the Sultan Muhammad IV Stadium on Friday.

The visitors wasted little time asserting their authority, breaking the deadlock in the 15th minute when Azfar found the back of the net with a clinical finish. Star City doubled their advantage right on the stroke of half-time through Brazilian Pedro Santos Filho before Azfar struck his second deep into first-half stoppage time to leave the hosts with a mountain to climb at 3-0 down.
Irfan Bakti Abu Salim's men attempted to muster a fightback after the break, pulling a goal back in the 52nd minute courtesy of Mohd Faudzi.
However, any hopes of a comeback were snuffed out on the hour mark when Azfar completed his treble with an emphatic finish to restore Star City's three-goal cushion.
KRW captain Arham Khussyairi Ab Wahab gave the home fans something to cheer in the 69th minute by trimming the deficit to 4-2, but Mehmet Durakovic's charges remained in firm control.

Second-half substitute Ramon Machado then put the final stamp on an emphatic night for the visitors, calmly converting a penalty deep into second-half injury time to wrap up all three points in style.

3d9cfda7546faa66: BENGALURU: Manchester City's players and supporters have grown closer since the club were found to have breached Premier League financial rules, head coach Enzo Maresca said on Friday, adding scrutiny had placed him under no additional stress.
An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.
"I think (City centre back and captain) Ruben Dias said people do not like City winning, so that is why we like to win. That is a good message for everyone," Maresca said at a news conference.
"Since the noise, from my personal point of view, I can see the fans, the club, the team more together, for sure.

"There is noise around the club but we need to try to make our noise. That means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow (against Ipswich). This is the way we can make our noise. A different kind of noise, we are not able to control that.
"I don't feel any kind of stress about the outside situation because it is something I don't control. I just focus on how we can try to win the next games."
City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday in their first match since the verdict before suffering a 4-2 home defeat by back-to-back Champions League winners Paris St Germain on Wednesday.
Maresca's side remain top of the Premier League with six wins from six matches and will look to bounce back from their midweek defeat when they host 10th-placed Ipswich Town on Saturday.
Asked whether he had sought advice from anyone outside the club to better understand the situation, Maresca said he had no need to do so.

"I spoke with the club a few times, they explained to me the situation, so the situation is very clear, and I trust the club 100%, I trust the people that run the club and this is the reason why I joined the club," the Italian said.
Former City manager Pep Guardiola attended the PSG match, and Maresca said he caught up with him afterwards.
Maresca was part of Guardiola's coaching staff during City's treble-winning campaign before successful managerial spells at Leicester City and Chelsea.

"We were talking about the game, the first half, the second half. He was very happy to be at the stadium and then very positive about things he had seen during the game... This will always be his house," Maresca added.

4e8ce74e91400dee: LONDON: Michael Carrick said Friday that Manchester United had "moved on" from Lisandro Martinez's outburst aimed at the club's hierarchy, stressing it was "really not a drama for us as a group."
Argentina defender Martinez took aim at the United hierarchy following their 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, saying Carrick had been left with an under-strength squad.

The centre-back criticised technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he had "100 percent" expected more investment during the summer transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season.
It is understood Martinez, who issued an apology on Thursday, has been fined for his outburst.
United manager Carrick confirmed during a pre-match press conference on Friday that Martinez would be in his squad for their Premier League match at bitter rivals Leeds on Sunday.
Carrick, under intense pressure after a terrible start to the season, was asked by reporters about Martinez's comments and subsequent developments.
"We've moved on from that, it was one of those things," he said. "I think Licha (Martinez) has come out and acknowledged the situation and as a group we've moved on.
"It's really not a drama for us as a group, I think the boys have trained really well. This morning there was a really good feeling around the squad."
Martinez, 28, said in a statement he had held positive talks with the club's leadership and Carrick.
"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity," he said in a post on Instagram.
"The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise."
'Emotion'
Former United captain Roy Keane has branded the situation at his former club "a bit of a circus."
Carrick was pressed by reporters on the nature of the apology from Martinez, which did not mention Wilcox by name.
"I think he (Martinez) has released his statement and he's realised he's made a mistake," said the United boss. "I think that's enough for all of us to move on with."
He added: "I understand the emotion at times. We ask for passion, we ask for emotion, we ask for fire and we ask for players to care.
"There's a way of doing that and that's already been acknowledged. We need to carry that. We need to carry that intensity and that willingness and that togetherness and that spirit and everything."
United have made their worst start to a league season in 40 years.
They are 13th in the Premier League, with just one win from six matches, but Carrick, a former United and England midfielder, deflected a question about the pressure on him personally.
"I don't need results, we all need results," he said. "It's not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me.
"Bigger than any player, anyone else who works at this football club. It always has been, and it's not about me."

943fb920e16c9dc6: PETALING JAYA: Public Bank Bhd could see its consolidated net assets and earnings per share fall by four sen following a HK$1.96 billion (RM1.1 billion) goodwill impairment at its Hong Kong-listed subsidiary.

The impairment is expected to contribute to Public Financial Holdings Ltd (PFHL) recording a net loss of between HK$1.9 billion and HK$2 billion for the financial year ending Dec 31 compared to a net profit of HK$80 million in 2025, The Edge reported.
The Hong Kong company said the impairment was driven by higher long-term interest rates, which increased the discount rate used to value goodwill, and weaker medium-term cash flow projections.

Rising funding costs were also squeezing net interest margins, as much of the group’s lending portfolio carries fixed interest rates or is linked to Hong Kong’s prime rate, which tends to remain stable across interest-rate cycles.
The impairment is a non-cash accounting item and will not affect the group’s operating cash flow.
Public Bank said the profit warning would have no operational impact on the bank or its other subsidiaries, although it could reduce consolidated net assets and earnings per share by four sen.
Nor will it affect the financial positions or regulatory capital ratios of its key Hong Kong operating subsidiaries, namely, Public Bank (Hong Kong) Ltd and Public Finance Ltd.
On a separate matter, Public Bank is seeking to privatise PFHL, where it holds a 73% stake, by acquiring the remaining 27% for HK$2.50 per share, or HK$734.75 million.
The proposed privatisation, announced last month, will be carried out through a court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement, with no increase in the offer price.
3c203c9854b8cde1: Legal experts are sounding alarms that Meta will soon update its commercial terms to require business accounts to allow Meta to train AI on their linked website content, not just their social media posts.

Kicking in on October 30, the TOS update won’t allow businesses to opt out, instead suggesting that businesses stop using Meta services if they won’t agree to let Meta bots freely crawl their linked content.

As Nieman Lab reported Thursday, this will affect all business accounts but is particularly shocking for news publishers who could perhaps charge Meta millions in licensing fees to continually access their articles for AI training. Currently news organizations are fighting a battle with OpenAI over whether such training without licensing is fair use, and Meta's terms seemingly risk granting it sweeping permissions, no matter which way the court leans.

James has suffered multiple injuries over the past few seasons, which have forced him to miss significant periods.
Last season, he enjoyed his best run of games for several years, culminating in his selection for England's 2026 World Cup squad.
The right-back was among the five players to withdraw from England duty during the most recent international break and now looks set to miss the next international window in November.
Chelsea are sixth in the Premier League after six matches of the season.

205340d307a13a6a: PETALING JAYA: Adun tidak sepatutnya turut memegang peranan Ahli Parlimen pada masa sama, kata Speaker DUN Sarawak Asfia Awang Nassar hari ini susulan pertikaman lidah berhubung penggantungan Ketua Pembangkang Chong Chieng Jen.

Usul berkenaan turut mendakwa beliau menggunakan kata-kata kesat serta menghina terhadap Adun lain selain mengaitkan mereka dengan niat jahat.

Shahrudin said investigations were ongoing to determine the cause of the explosion, the source of the materials used and whether others were involved
The case is investigated under Section 8 of the Explosives Act.

c49e949ebeec733c: THERE seems to be an almost insatiable demand for scrap metal. And not just locally. It started many years ago.

There was even an international dimension that traced such demand all the way to China. Thus, local councils have been hard put to keep metal covers for manholes and drains in place, among other things.

The raging fire in Pasir Gudang, Johor, in recent days is said to be deliberately started by cable thieves seeking to separate scrap metal from piles of wood. The blaze has spread to an area of 1.4ha. Firefighters were still battling it some 19 hours later.

This is a stark reminder that theft is not merely a property crime when criminals are willing to put lives, the environment and public safety at risk just so they can get their hands on ill-gotten goods.
These cannot be isolated cases. The authorities need to see them for what they are: networks, organised syndicates and weak enforcement coming together for such activities to persist.
There is a worrying pattern of recklessness involved here. In recent days, cable thefts have disrupted critical infrastructure, including the KLIA Ekspres and KLIA Transit services.
The common thread is criminals helping themselves to materials for their resale value, with total disregard for the consequences to and convenience and safety of the wider public.
What appears as cost-free quick profit for the thieves will translate into disrupted services, costly repairs and replacements, environmental damage and even risks to human lives.
Any foolproof solutions must target the market for such ill-gotten materials, not just the thieves involved. Enforcement must not stop with arresting those caught stealing.

The authorities must root out the supply chain by identifying and shaming scrap dealers who knowingly purchase stolen materials and take firm action against buyers providing the outlet for such looted goods.

Absent a ready market, the incentive to steal will be substantially reduced. The police, local authorities, government agencies and scrap metal industry players must work together to improve traceability, verify the origins of the materials and single out suspicious transactions.
Licensing and inspection regimens must be consistently enforced, with painful penalties imposed on businesses complicit in facilitating the trade in stolen goods.

Consequences for those caught must be fully proportionate to the harm caused. Investigations into the Johor blaze must establish its cause as well as the extent of responsibility of all those involved.
Where criminal wrongdoing is evident, the prosecution and penalties ought to reflect not only the severity of the crime, but also any additional and related offences and damage caused.

eedb0ea5eb998cd8: The October 2026 Windows security update may break networking for some customers who are still clinging to long-deprecated NTLMv1 security. A seemingly minor change in the update could have major implications for administrators and enterprises that haven't fully moved away from the legacy technology. Before the October 2026 update, Windows permitted NTLMv1-derived credentials for Single Sign-On and generated warning events. After the update, requests to use NTLMv1-derived credentials are blocked. It comes down to the BlockNtlmSSO registry value. If it hasn't been set, Windows will now use Enforce mode (1) instead of Audit mode (0), thus blocking requests and potentially impacting Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and VPN authentication, and therefore connections. The update does not set the value of BlockNtlmSSO, and administrators can set it to 0 to temporarily allow NTLMv1-derived Single Sign-On credentials. However, Microsoft noted, "Using Audit mode reduces the protection provided by Enforce mode and should only be considered as a scoped, temporary security exception." To be clear, this is not a bug and is by design. The addition of NTLM to the deprecation list occurred in 2024, and Microsoft added audit logs for NTLMv1 usage in late August 2025. The Windows giant has made no secret of its desire to ditch the legacy technology, stating in 2023, "Our end goal is eliminating the need to use NTLM at all." The problem is NTLM's longevity. It appeared in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1, and removing it from enterprise environments has proven tricky, even though it is somewhat insecure by modern standards. Microsoft removed it from Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025, but some remnants can still be found, notably when using MS-CHAPv2-based connections, including PEAP-MSCHAPv2, and EAP-MSCHAPv2, in a domain-joined environment. Hence the introduction of the audit mode in 2025, to help administrators spot where the technology was still being used. It is now 2026, and Microsoft has taken the next step. If Credential Guard is not enabled and BlockNtlmSSO is not set to Audit mode (0), the use of NTLMv1-derived credentials will be blocked as Microsoft works "to finalize the disablement of NTLMv1." There is no indication of how long the BlockNtlmSSO workaround (setting the value to Audit mode) will work - most likely until the next major Windows release. In September, Microsoft said, "In-market versions of Windows client and Windows Server will continue to support NTLM." However, it also stated, "Our long-term objective is a Windows platform that doesn't need NTLM at all." As such, if the message wasn't already clear, the move to enforce it by default makes it impossible to miss. The technology still exists in the operating system, but it is on its way out and will be removed in a future Windows release. Problems with networking after the October 2026 Windows security update could therefore signal that migration plans are not as far along, or as complete, as administrators might have thought. ®

5d66d63c164ca86e: PETALING JAYA: Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Ismail Lasim should resign after he was publicly admonished by the state’s ruler earlier today, a senior lawyer said.

“Resign and repent - this is the least that Ismail can do to redeem himself," Rosli told FMT.

Rosli accused Ismail of having “shamelessly” taken his oath of office as menteri besar before Tuanku Muhriz on Aug 2, only to sign a proclamation made months before to denounce Tuanku Muhriz as having been dethroned.

Tuanku Muhriz’s rebuke of Ismail comes amid a constitutional crisis in the state sparked in April after four persons claiming to be undangs, or traditional chieftains, announced the purported removal of Tuanku Muhriz as the state’s ruler, and proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar as the Yang Dipertuan Besar.

1c4e26bb56e5c8c8: DONALD Trump is crisscrossing America to drum up votes for Republican candidates facing tough midterm election races, but the United States president's rallies are often hijacked by his basking in the adulation of fervent supporters.

Journalists followed him on Tuesday and Wednesday during one such trip out West, a rapid succession of flights and rallies — in a glacial valley in Alaska, on an arid plain in Arizona and in the forests of Montana.
The Republican leader is betting on his ability to mobilise voters despite polls predicting that his party will lose control of one or both chambers of Congress on Nov 3.
A Fox News poll released on Thursday puts his approval rating at just 36 per cent, a new low, largely because of growing dissatisfaction over the cost of living.
"Please pretend that I am on the ballot," the 80-year-old leader, wearing a red cap, told the crowd Wednesday in Bullhead City, Arizona.

In 2024, he got nearly 78 per cent of the vote in the county where he was speaking in Arizona. The other two counties he visited, in Alaska and Montana, also gave him decisive victories over Democrat Kamala Harris.
Trump makes no secret of his preference for travelling to friendly territory, telling reporters that he wants to "pay my respect" to supporters.
"We brought back the spirit" of the 2024 presidential campaign, he declared. It is difficult to judge.
Each appearance drew committed supporters, the core of his MAGA (Make America Great Again) movement, who are apparently willing to forgive him for soaring fuel prices as well as the war in Iran.
"The country needs to be a little bit more patient," Theresa Hallesy said on Wednesday in Montana.
"There's a lot of stuff going on in the world that he can't control, but he still has to deal with it. I think we're going in the right direction."
The 68-year-old retiree waited more than seven hours for Trump to make his entrance into a large rodeo arena commandeered for the occasion.
The American president is rallying support for his party, but he seemed almost reluctant to invite local candidates to join him onstage during the tour.

"I want you just to come up for one minute because we don't want to hear you for two minutes, three minutes, just one minute," he told Andy Biggs, a conservative seeking to become governor of Arizona.
The Republican leader always has one or two announcements tailored to each region.
In Alaska on Tuesday, at a hockey rink converted into a rally venue, he laid out his climate-sceptic arguments.
In a state whose economy is closely tied to fossil fuels, Trump promoted a major liquefied natural gas project.
He also issued presidential pardons for two auto mechanics who were convicted of modifying diesel engines to circumvent emissions regulations.
At each rally, he promised that every American will receive US$5,000 if Republicans retain their majorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate.
How this highly controversial proposal, criticised by the opposition, would be funded remains unclear.
Yet rather than an electoral offensive, his rallies give the impression of a final tour for a show whose star performer and audience are already feeling nostalgic.

In Montana, thousands of enthusiastic supporters laughed at a now-familiar impersonation of French President Emmanuel Macron and gave Trump a standing ovation as he left the stage, dancing to the ever-present strains of YMCA.
In Arizona, the billionaire delighted the audience with a flyover by the new presidential aircraft, a lavish gift from Qatar.
Onstage, he joked about the present, estimated to be worth US$400 million: "You know, when you are given gifts, you take them, right?"
The joke fell somewhat flat with the audience in a district where both the poverty rate and the unemployment rate are significantly above the national average.
The Republican leader then spoke regretfully about the approaching end of his term, saying he has resigned himself to it in "2½ years. Now a little less than that, sadly."
"I said that yesterday and they started screaming, 'Four more years! Four more years!'" Trump continued.
He paused. He waited. The audience eventually took the cue, and a few voices broke into the chant, "Four more years! Four more years!" — without much conviction.

619dbdcf855cf5ac: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal three-member panel today reserved its decision on blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris's appeal against the High Court's decision which sentenced him to 30 days in jail for contempt of court in a defamation suit filed by former Inspector-General of Polis Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid.
Justice Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan who chaired the three-member panel fixed Oct 29 for case management to set the date for the decision.
Earlier the panel, also comprising Justices Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun, heard submissions by lawyers representing Azri and Razarudin respectively.
On Aug 27, 2025, High Court Judicial Commissioner Gan Techiong ruled that Azri, also known as Papagomo, had breached a court injunction concerning the ongoing defamation suit filed by Razarudin.

Gan sentenced the blogger to 15 days in jail for failing to properly comply with the court order to apologise to Razarudin, and another 15 days for making a statement in the video which showed a lack of remorse.

The High Court had ordered the custodial sentences to run consecutively and Azri was also ordered to pay Razarudin RM30,000 in costs. However, the court granted Azri a stay of execution of the sentence pending his appeal.

At the hearing of the appeal in the Court of Appeal today, Azri's lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali submitted that his client was not in contempt of court as he had complied with the terms of the court order by reading the agreed unconditional apology to the court and to Razarudin in open court on April 30, 2025 and deleted the earlier publications.

Rafique said Azri had also complied with the court's directive to publish the same apology on his four social media accounts for at least seven days and had paid RM5,000 in costs as well as his apology was widely reported by the media.
Alternatively, he submitted that jail term imposed on his client should be substituted with a fine.
However, lawyer Raam Kumar representing Razarudin, urged the court to uphold the two contempt orders made by the High Court.

He submitted that Azri failed to genuinely comply with the apology, adding the apology was presented in a manner that made it difficult to read and it was not shown to have been maintained on his relevant social media platforms.

Raam, assisted by Tan Khay Boon and Norleena Jamal further said under Section 69(4) of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964, the court has the power to increase the sentence even if there is no cross-appeal regarding it.
Razarudin filed a RM3 million defamation suit against Azri on Dec 27, 2024 over allegedly defamatory remarks involving him and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
On Jan 10, 2025, Razarudin obtained an injunction prohibiting Azri or his agents from publishing or disseminating defamatory statements about him on social media until disposal of the civil suit.
The High Court had scheduled to hear the contempt of court proceedings initiated by Razarudin on April 30, last year. However, Azri decided to apologise to Razarudin and to the court.

820761748dafb78b: THERE is a good reason why after starting off with daily flights from Kuching to Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, the next destination for the Sarawak-owned AirBorneo is Jakarta.
Although AirAsia now flies daily between Kuching and Jakarta, AirBorneo is positioning itself as a premium carrier.
The existing Kuching-Jakarta flights are popular and it is not unusual to see at least a few passengers needing wheelchairs to board and disembark on each flight.

Kuching has successfully tapped into the lucrative Indonesian medical tourism market and the direct flight from Jakarta takes only 1½ hours, making the Sarawak capital the nearest Malaysian city to the Indonesian capital.

The private hospitals in Kuching have for some time already made a name for themselves with residents from West Kalimantan, and it is believed that Kuching's reputation for reasonably affordable and quality medical care had mostly spread by word-of-mouth to Jakarta residents, from kith and kin in the Borneo province bordering Sarawak.
Such Indonesian medical tourists to Kuching will be even more spoilt for choice as at least two new hospitals are currently under construction.
The 200-bed Gleneagles Hospital Kuching will open in 2028 while the Regency Specialist Hospital Kuching is a 300-bed facility scheduled to open in 2029.
Private healthcare in Kuching was pioneered by the Normah Medical Specialist Centre some 35 years ago.

Three state agencies — the Sarawak Economic Development Corporation, the Sarawak Electricity Supply Corporation and the Sarawak Timber Industry Development Corporation — pooled resources to build this facility.
Since then, two more local private hospitals — Timberland Medical Centre and Borneo Medical Centre — have been set up and are expanding their facilities.
The KPJ Kuching Specialist Hospital rounds up the presently operating four private hospitals in Kuching.

Competition for market share can be expected to go up several notches once the two facilities under construction become operational. It will mean three homegrown establishments vying for clients against three others with international links.
Normah Medical Specialist Centre, especially, may be ripe for reviewing its setup.
There was a justification for state-led involvement in its establishment decades earlier when the market for private medical centres was untested.
There is less of a reason for it to invest in a new, planned facility if it involves more public funds.
In light of this increased competition, the hospital should re-examine its strategic position and consider how it will compete in the private healthcare industry of the future.
A comprehensive review of its comparative advantages, service offerings, technological capabilities and long-term growth prospects will be beneficial.
As Sarawak develops further, local demand for private health care can be expected to rise so as to avoid an unhealthy over-dependence on demand from across the border.

It is perhaps an opportune time as well for Normah Medical Specialist Centre and the other private hospitals to explore ways to up their game, such as gaining international accreditation in order to widen the pool of international patients.

The state still has a long way to go as its RM300 million medical tourism revenue a year is only a fraction of the reported RM3.5 billion annual revenue nationally and even pales in comparison with Penang's RM1.5 billion annual take.

6abb14faab34b7cd: The next 200-megawatt data center permitted in your county probably won't look like the buildings you remember from a decade ago. It will occupy the footprint of two or three football fields and draw more power than most nearby industrial parks combined. It will also likely trigger a town hall meeting before the first pad is poured. That collision between AI-driven demand and physical reality is what NTT Global Data Centers set out to quantify in its new AI Stress Test Report. The report models three growth trajectories through 2030 and stress-tests each against the constraints operators hit, such as land availability, water consumption, specialized labor and more. The middle (baseline) scenario projects annual demand growth of about 23 percent, which pencils out to roughly $3.8 trillion of additional investment in digital infrastructure. Ramp to the accelerated case and the figure climbs to $5.7 trillion. Bruno Berti, CTO at NTT Global Data Centers, notes that he has watched the size envelope stretch beyond recognition. "We used to build ten-megawatt buildings, smaller buildings, to support some of these applications," says Berti. "But now we're building buildings that are hundreds of megawatts, double the size, sizes of two, maybe sometimes three football fields." Why permitting became the choke point Ask most operators what will bottleneck AI infrastructure and you'll hear GPUs, transformers, switchgear. NTT Global Data Centers’ stress test suggests something more mundane: paperwork, planning and process. Power availability and deployment timelines, not fiber capacity, are the gating factors in the scenarios modeled. Berti puts it plainly: it doesn't matter how quickly you can get GPUs if you can't get a permit to put them anywhere. That reframes the strategy question. Berti argues against a "build, baby, build" reflex, preferring a portfolio approach that treats capacity expansion as a system-wide coordination problem rather than a land race. The misconceptions that stall projects Two objections come up in almost every community consultation, according to Berti: data centers waste water, and they steal power from the grid. Both are misconceptions and come from an older generation of facilities. Modern designs, he says, use liquid cooling technology, which removes heat more effectively, eliminating excess water waste. Additionally, operators plan the new class of hundred-megawatt-plus sites in partnership with utilities years in advance, often with on-site solar, wind or other renewable generation that can help stabilize the grid rather than drain it. His conclusion is blunt: transparency builds trust. So, the industry has to stop treating what it does as a secret and start to build that trust through education and partnership if it wants the permits it will need through the decade to turn capacity into reliable AI infrastructure that can benefit communities, policymakers and businesses alike. Sponsored by NTT Global Data Centers.
1e9649918da5b400: MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional's (BN) Melaka election candidates have been finalised and could be announced at any time, says state BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
The Melaka chief minister said he would not take long to announce the candidates, with nomination day approaching.

"The entire list of candidates is ready. We will announce it soon... at any time," he said briefly after attending the Sembang Santai Geng E-Hailing dan P-Hailing programme in Kampung Pulau here tonight.
He also dismissed claims that BN's candidates would be announced on Oct 24.
"Who said that (Oct 24)? Ask the person who said it. It did not come from me."
Ab Rauf said BN's preparations were in the final stages, including negotiations with coalition partners to finalise cooperation and the distribution of seats to be contested.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, enabling it to form the state government on its own before Pakatan Harapan (PH) later joined the state administration.
Ab Rauf said the outcome of negotiations with coalition partners would also be announced ahead of nomination day.
"The outcome of the negotiations will be announced after the final round of talks in the near future," he said.
df993b78a683cf7c: KUALA LUMPUR: A viral video showing Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail solemnising a civil marriage between a non-Muslim couple was recorded in 2023, the National Registration Department (NRD) said.
The department said the video was part of its Diamond Jubilee celebration held in conjunction with National Registration Day that year, and the matter had already been clarified on Oct 25 that year.

"NRD takes seriously the recirculation of the video clip of the home minister solemnising a civil marriage between a non-Muslim couple, despite the matter having been officially clarified since Oct 25, 2023.

"Recycling old footage without explaining the actual context, particularly when it creates a misleading perception, is irresponsible and could cause misunderstandings among the public," it said in a statement.
The department said it was responsible for registering civil marriages between non-Muslim couples under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act.
It added that Saifuddin's involvement in solemnising the marriage was part of the department's official programme in 2023 and should be understood in the context of its legal functions.
NRD also said it had sought views from the Federal Territories Mufti Department on relevant aspects of Islamic law.
It said the public to rely on facts and explanations from the relevant authorities rather than assumptions or misleading interpretations.
"Differences of opinion should not be used as a reason to disseminate information out of context and trigger unfounded controversy," it said.
b93d68b908a163e1: KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has defended the government's decision to grant Malaysian citizenship to foreign footballers, revealing that the applicants were coached in basic Malay before interviews, and could have their time overseas counted as residency in Malaysia.

Speaking during a townhall session at UiTM Kedah on Tuesday, Saifuddin said the Home Ministry acted within the Federal Constitution when approving citizenship applications under Article 19, which covers naturalisation.
His remarks come amid continued scrutiny of the citizenship process following sanctions imposed by FIFA on the FA of Malaysia (FAM) over falsified documents involving seven foreign-born players.

Saifuddin acknowledged that the applicants from countries such as Argentina had not lived in Malaysia for the required period, but said the Home Minister had constitutional powers to grant exemptions.
"He is from Argentina. Was there any period of residing in this country? The answer is no," Saifuddin told the audience.

"However, under the Federal Constitution, the Home Minister can grant an exemption. That means the period he was in Argentina or Spain can be considered as residing in our country. This is the Federal Constitution, not something Saifuddin made up."
On the requirement for applicants to have "adequate knowledge of the Malay language", Saifuddin said the law did not require fluency, describing the standard as subjective.

"Adequate knowledge is subjective. Typically, for this category, our practice is that we coach them before the interview: 'Apa khabar?' (How are you?), they answer 'Khabar baik' (I am well). 'Terima kasih' (Thank you), they answer 'Sama-sama' (You are welcome). That is the current practice," he said.
"It does not say fluent, nor does it require in-depth knowledge. It says adequate. If they understand, we pass them," he added.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry's responsibility ended once the citizenship process, which includes police security clearance, language assessment and administrative approval, was completed.
"Whether he can play for Malaysia or not, that is FAM's business. Whatever documents FAM submits to register with FIFA, that is their affair, not the Home Ministry's.

"Whether they qualify or what documents FAM sent to FIFA is no longer my responsibility. Can I answer on behalf of FAM? No, because that falls under FIFA's charter. Let their president answer that," he added.

The controversy erupted in September last year when FIFA found that FAM had used falsified documents to establish the eligibility of seven foreign-born players to represent Malaysia. The players — Gabriel Palmero, Facundo Garces, Rodrigo Holgado, Imanol Machuca, Joao Figueiredo, Jon Irazabal and Hector Hevel — had featured in Malaysia's 4-0 win over Vietnam in a 2027 Asian Cup qualifier on June 10, 2025, among others.

FIFA fined FAM CHF350,000 (about RM1.8 million) and handed each player a 12-month suspension. The Court of Arbitration for Sport later ruled in March that the suspensions would apply only to official matches, allowing the players to continue training and taking part in other football-related activities. The 12-month bans are due to reach their end later this month.

The case has continued to draw attention to FAM's handling of player eligibility documents and the process used to grant citizenship to foreign-born footballers. FAM president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan said last month that he would meet Saifuddin to seek clarification on the players' citizenship and passport status, as the matter falls outside the football body's jurisdiction.

With the players nearing the end of their suspensions, the scandal continues to cast a shadow over Malaysian football, raising questions about accountability, citizenship approval and the steps needed to restore confidence in Harimau Malaya.
a7b158486227792a: NEW DELHI: Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday ahead of fresh protests demanding the removal of the country's election chief, the youth-led movement said in a social media post.
Dipke, 31, was detained shortly before a protest called by the online movement at Central Park in Connaught Place, a busy commercial district in the heart of New Delhi.
"Abhijeet is detained by Delhi Police!!! This government is so scared of the youth waving national flag!!," the CJP said on social media.

The group as well as opposition parties have been seeking the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a large-scale voter roll revision that they say favours prime minister Narendra Modi's ruling party.
The Election Commission of India, which oversees voting in the world's most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.

Dipke had urged supporters to carry national flags and gather at Central Park after two of his colleagues were detained for breaching security barricades at Jantar Mantar, a protest site declared off-limits by police this week.
Thousands of security personnel were deployed in central Delhi on Friday, with police warning protesters to stay away, citing orders restricting public gatherings.
In the past week, the Indian capital has seen several street protests against the electoral roll revision, which was overseen by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
More than 133 million names have been removed from electoral lists under the exercise, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings.
Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.
3bb0944e9a55f257: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has wished the Malaysian contingent success at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games in Japan from Oct 18 to 24.

The national contingent is targeting six gold, 10 silver and 16 bronze medals across athletics, badminton and boccia.
e46c59460f838141: KUALA BERANG: Mayat seorang bayi tanpa kepala dan satu tangan ditemukan di dalam longkang di kawasan perumahan di Kampung Padang Setengge, petang tadi.
Ketua Polis Hulu Terengganu, Sharudin Abdul Wahab, berkata pihaknya menerima laporan daripada orang awam berhubung penemuan itu pada 6.52 petang.
Susulan laporan berkenaan, polis menghubungi unit forensik dan unit K9 IPK Terengganu untuk membantu siasatan serta mengumpul bukti di lokasi kejadian.
"Mayat bayi itu ditemukan oleh seorang wanita ketika membasuh pakaian di belakang rumahnya. Ketika ditemukan, mayat berkenaan berada dalam keadaan tanpa kepala dan satu tangan," menurut kenyataan.
Setakat ini, polis belum dapat mengenal pasti jantina dan kewarganegaraan bayi berkenaan. Mayat dihantar ke Jabatan Forensik Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah untuk bedah siasat.
Kes disiasat mengikut Seksyen 318 Kanun Keseksaan.
Polis meminta orang ramai yang mempunyai maklumat berkaitan kejadian itu supaya menghubungi balai polis berhampiran bagi membantu siasatan.
893315e9467cfbe7: KUALA BERANG: The body of a baby, missing its head and one hand, was found in a drain behind a house in Kampung Padang Setengge here this evening.
Hulu Terengganu police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said police received a report on the discovery at 6.52pm.
He said the baby was found by a woman who was washing clothes behind her house.
"The baby's body was found without its head and missing one hand.

"So far, police have been unable to determine the baby's sex or nationality. The body has been sent to the Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital's Forensic Department for a post-mortem," he said in a statement.
Sharudin said the D10 forensic unit and K9 unit from the Terengganu police contingent headquarters had been called in to assist with investigations and gather evidence at the scene.
The case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code.
Members of the public with information about the incident are urged to contact the nearest police station.
3c5c586d6ac92920: PETALING JAYA: Assemblymen should not double up as MPs, Sarawak state assembly speaker Asfia Awang Nassar said today following an exchange over the suspension of opposition leader Chong Chieng Jen.

The argument was sparked after Pending assemblyman, Violet Yong of DAP, said it was unfair for Asfia to say that Chong had chosen not to attend the sitting. She said Asfia "knew very well” that Chong, who is Stampin MP, was at the Dewan Rakyat for a parliamentary matter, yet Asfia allowed the motions against him at the state assembly to proceed.

Yong then accused Asfia of denying Chong’s right to defence, which was, embarrassingly, against the principle of natural justice. In response, Asfia said Yong and Chong, who is also Padungan assemblyman, came to see him seeking an exemption, to which he agreed.

“But the procedure is it must be in writing through the secretary,” Asfia said in a video posted on Sarawak DAP’s Facebook page today. However, Asfia said Chong had attacked him on Facebook over the Hansard, a post which gave him the impression that Chong was in Sarawak.
Yong, however, argued that despite Chong’s action, it did not give the speaker the right to say that he “chose to be absent”.

“Don’t say that. You can say ‘I don’t know why he is absent today’, but you don’t say he chose to be absent. So Mr Speaker be more polite. Please be fair to the opposition and don’t be so tilted in your ruling and in your argument. I know you are trying to be in the good books of GPS,” she said, referring to the state’s ruling coalition, Gabungan Parti Sarawak.
In response, Asfia shot back: “Don’t be an MP and an assemblyman at the same time if you don’t have the time.”

Chong, who is also Sarawak DAP chief, was suspended from the state assembly yesterday for the remainder of the current session after a motion was adopted alleging that he misled the assembly about Sarawak’s 2027 budget document and acted improperly during its debate.

The motion alleged that Chong deliberately misled the assembly on Oct 13 and acted improperly during the budget debate on Oct 14, by repeatedly making allegations he could not substantiate. It accused him of using offensive and insulting language against fellow assemblymen and imputing improper motives to them.
c6cf8e5bed01e3e9: KUALA LUMPUR: National Songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza shocked fans on social media after revealing minor facial injuries—just ahead of her highly anticipated Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil tomorrow.
In a snapshot shared on her official Instagram account this afternoon, the country's top entertainer displayed a small cut near her right eye alongside visible bruising across her cheek.
"Bismillah, may everything be made easy. See you tomorrow, my dear Sitizoners!" she wrote in a brief caption accompanying the post, immediately sparking anxiety among her followers.
Many fans flooded the comments section with speculation that the injuries occurred during intense rehearsals leading up to the grand showcase.
The powerhouse vocalist is no stranger to daring performances.

During her Legacy 30 Siti Nurhaliza: Passion, Sincere and Love concert in January, the mother of two stunned attendees by performing her hit single Purnama Merindu while elevated on a crane, as well as performing a breathtaking high jump entrance from underneath the stage.
Reflecting on her upcoming show, Siti described the Gema Bumantara concert as a monumental milestone in an illustrious career spanning more than three decades.
She emphasised that the event was not just entertainment, acting as a crucial platform to unite champions of traditional tunes who continue to preserve the nation's musical heritage.
She added that having Malaysia's Queen of Traditional Pop, Noraniza Idris, as a guest artiste was essential.
The duo famously collaborated on the hit track Hati Kama from their joint 1999 album Seri Balas under Suria Records.
Alongside Noraniza Idris, Konsert Traditional Gema Bumantara will also feature rising traditional singer Haziq Rosebi, as well as Indonesian music stars King Nassar and Lesti Kejora.
32e9e14905783aeb: KOTA BARU: Amanah has been allocated eight state seats to contest in the Melaka election, subject to final approval by Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also agriculture and food security minister, said the allocation was the outcome of discussions at the PH level.
However, he said the final decision would be made by the PH presidential council on Oct 24.

"As of now, at the PH level, we have been allocated eight seats, but we have not yet finalised our contesting model. We will finalise the matter in the presidential council and announce it on Oct 24," he told reporters after attending the 2026 Kelantan Amanah Convention here today.
Mohamad said the actual number of seats Amanah would contest could depend on broader cooperation arrangements that were still under discussion.
The Election Commission has set Oct 31 for nomination, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling in the Melaka election, following the dissolution of the state assembly on Sept 23.
564172d9e00b7b23: KUALA LUMPUR: A leaked FIFA letter revealed that KL City have been slapped with a new transfer ban over unpaid money owed to its former player, Patrick Reichelt, of the Philippines.
The letter, dated Oct 15, which was sent from FIFA's legal hub in Miami, was widely shared on social media and messaging apps yesterday.
Signed by FIFA head of disciplinary Americo Espallargas, the document confirmed that KL City had failed to comply with an earlier ruling in favour of the 38-year-old Reichelt.
"In this context, it appears that, despite the Decision, Kuala Lumpur City FC (the Respondent) has not yet complied with its financial obligations towards Patrick Reichelt," the letter stated.
As the salary remained unpaid, FIFA imposed a ban preventing the City Boys from registering new players.

"In this regard, we wish to inform the parties that a ban from registering new players internationally and nationally has been implemented by FIFA on the Respondent," the letter read, adding that the ban would "remain active until the amount due is paid and for a maximum duration of up to three entire and consecutive registration periods."
FIFA also directed the FA of Malaysia to take action, requesting the national body to "immediately implement on the Respondent a ban from registering new players at national level, if not done yet."
The development comes just two months after KLFA president Syed Yazid Syed Omar announced in August that KL City had paid close to RM1 million to settle outstanding cases.

Before that, transfer bans caused registration delays that left KL City unable to register enough players for their Super League opener against Negri Sembilan. The match was called off, Negri were awarded a 3-0 win, and the Malaysian Football League fined KL City RM50,000.
Days later, KL City had to face Kuching City with only 10 players on the pitch, one substitute and no reserve goalkeeper. They suffered a 6-0 defeat.

The club's financial problems date back several years. In 2024, KL City were deducted six league points, fined RM100,000 and stripped of their AFC club licence after failing to make proper payments to the Employees Provident Fund, Socso and the Inland Revenue Board.
Neither KL City nor FAM has issued an official statement on the leaked letter.

In March, forward Reichelt spoke of what he described as a "culture of hiding debts" in Malaysian football, claiming KL City had paid only 40 per cent of the money owed to him from six months of unpaid wages dating back to 2023.
da465de3b23b1d9b: KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed deep concern over the health and education of children following the haze affecting the country.
