"Her Majesty's concern serves as a guide in our efforts to ensure that every decision concerning school operations takes into account children's health and educational future comprehensively," she said.
581ec22677ea2f85: The FBI is once again warning US citizens to be on the lookout for the scams that are so often rife around election season. With November’s midterms fast approaching, the FBI said scammers are known to use the names, imagery, and slogans of high-profile candidates for a range of frauds. These are often related to making donations and selling merchandise, but can also be geared toward stealing personal data for use in follow-on scams. And of course, more recently, fraudsters’ efforts can be all the more convincing given the rise in AI use and deepfake technology, which can also be used to more accurately imitate the likenesses of candidates and other officials. Campaign investment pool schemes are among the four big frauds the FBI wants the public to watch out for over the next few weeks. These involve scammers convincing their marks to pay into a campaign pool, which ostensibly pays out to all of those who donated after the candidate wins. More commonly, these types of pooled investment scams are based on collective investments into stocks and other appreciating assets. The FBI did not provide details about these campaign pools’ investment incentives or how victims are supposedly able to increase their stake by donating to the cause, but did say that no genuine campaign donations appreciate over time. Another common donation-based scam to be wary of is the one that convinces victims to fund a fake political action committee (PAC), one that collects supporters’ cash and promises to hand it to their favored party or candidate. Instead of forwarding money to a specific political campaign, however, the scammers pocket it all for themselves. Fraudsters are also known for claiming to sell merchandise related to political campaigns – orders that ultimately go unfulfilled. These constitute non-delivery scams, which rank in the top five genres of internet cons, according to the Internet Crime Complaint Center’s (IC3) most recent annual report. The same report put phishing at the number one spot in that same list, and the classic cyberattack features on the FBI’s list of midterm-related scams, too. Creating a sense of urgency, scammers will text victims claiming they have not yet registered to vote, and asking them to follow a link to a webpage where they can enter their details and complete the process, which of course leads to identity theft. While the FBI doesn’t include this detail in its advisory, Texans should be especially wary of these communication attempts given the recent computer issues that led to a massive backlog in registration applications. As of September 22, 226, around 600,000 applications were allegedly in limbo after a website flaw failed to record voters’ intentions to vote, and therefore did not receive registration forms from the Texas Secretary of State (SOS), according to a lawsuit [PDF] filed by voter registration organizations last week. However, spokesperson for the SOS’ office Alicia Pierce told USA Today that the backlog was only in the tens of thousands and that as of this week it was all-clear. Scammers may nevertheless continue to capitalize on the public awareness of the backlog when devising the lures for their phishing campaigns. The feds advised the public to be wary of these kinds of communications, and verify all political organizations, such as PACs, via the government’s election commission website. Although some scam PACs can appear on the website as registered, you can usually discern the suspicious ones when they report high expenses for matters such as consulting, fundraising, and other admin costs. The FBI's advisory follows separate action taken by X, which on Wednesday evening warned that influence campaigns originating from Iran, Russia, and China were targeting US voters, amplifying content across the political spectrum. The social media platform responded by nuking more than 13,000 accounts linked to the foreign interference attempts. ®
2044ebb2bd8c32d0: KUALA LUMPUR: Proklamasi bertarikh 19 April 2026 yang bertujuan menurunkan Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir daripada takhta namun ditolak oleh Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) gagal mematuhi kehendak Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS), menurut Majlis Peguam.

Presiden Anand Raj berkata Perkara 10(1) UUTKNS mensyaratkan siasatan menyeluruh dan lengkap oleh para Undang sebelum mereka boleh menggesa pemerintah untuk menarik diri daripada menjalankan fungsi-fungsi baginda atau turun takhta.
Beliau berkata sebarang 'siasatan sewajarnya' di bawah Perkara 10 UUTKNS perlu mematuhi kehendak perlembagaan dan prinsip keadilan asasi.

"Selain kesahihan proklamasi yang didakwa itu dan pengeluarannya (yang menurut AGC adalah tidak sah), tiada rekod semasa yang dikeluarkan untuk membuktikan bahawa siasatan sebegitu pernah dijalankan, atau bahawa Kebawah Duli Yang Maha Mulia pernah diberikan peluang untuk menangkis dakwaan terhadap baginda," menurut kenyataan.

Anand berkata hak untuk didengar adalah prinsip asas keadilan asasi, yang memerlukan seseorang yang didakwa melakukan salah laku mengetahui kes terhadapnya dan diberi peluang yang adil untuk memberi maklum balas sebelum keputusan yang memudaratkan dibuat.

Merujuk kepada keputusan Jawatankuasa Kehakiman Majlis Privy dalam kes B Surinder Singh Kanda lawan kerajaan persekutuan Tanah Melayu [1962] 1 MLJ 169, beliau berkata prinsip itu terpakai kepada semua orang termasuk ketua negara.
"Jika warganegara biasa dilindungi secara perlembagaan daripada pemecatan tidak sah tanpa pendengaran yang adil, Kebawah Duli Yang Maha Mulia juga berhak mendapat perlindungan serupa," katanya.

Beliau berkata kegagalan mematuhi Perkara 10(1) UUTKNS menjadikan sebarang tindakan bagi menurunkan Tuanku Muhriz daripada takhta adalah tidak sah, sambil menambah mahkamah boleh membatalkan keputusan itu yang dicapai dengan mencabuli prinsip keadilan asasi.

Anand turut mengemukakan beberapa persoalan mengenai pengurusan krisis itu, termasuk tindakan menteri besar semasa mengumumkan perkara tersebut pada 16 Sept lepas berdasarkan proklamasi berkenaan meskipun pendahulunya secara terbuka menyifatkannya sebagai tidak sah.
Beliau berkata menteri besar itu juga mendakwa telah menandatangani proklamasi tersebut di bawah tekanan dan paksaan seperti yang dinyatakan dalam laporan polis pada 8 Sept lepas.

"Orang ramai berhak mengetahui siapa yang melakukannya, bagaimana dan mengapa ia berlaku serta mengapa beliau hanya membuat laporan polis pada 8 Sept, iaitu kira-kira lima minggu selepas proklamasi yang didakwa itu dikeluarkan," katanya.
Beliau berkata penjelasan juga diperlukan berhubung sebab menteri besar itu kemudian mengesahkan proklamasi berkenaan.
Anand berkata asas operasi kerajaan negeri juga mungkin memerlukan penjelasan kerana Tuanku Muhriz telah membatalkan pelantikan semua ahli majlis mesyuarat kerajaan negeri.

Majlis Peguam turut mengambil maklum kenyataan Majlis Raja-Raja Melayu pada 14 Okt lepas yang menyeru agar sebarang perbezaan pendapat diselesaikan mengikut adat dan undang-undang serta berpandukan peruntukan dalam undang-undang tubuh kerajaan negeri.
aaf5ed21973e0ad9: Prediction market boosters often tout the platforms as barometers of public opinion, or even “truth machines” offering a clearer picture of where things are headed than polling or other data. In 2024, for example, Kalshi beat many pollsters in forecasting the outcome of the US presidential race. But their trading activity can also tell more perplexing stories.

Two global election markets on Polymarket’s offshore platform, for instance, generated over $600 million in trading volume, far more than most political markets typically attract. Most of the activity took place buying and selling contracts tied to long-shot candidates who ultimately did not win.

This summer, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party cruised to victory in federal elections, winning 438 parliamentary seats and paving the way for him to serve another five-year term. The closest competitor won 13 seats. On prediction markets, trading volume—the total value of contracts bought and sold—typically tracks roughly with the odds of a given outcome; frontrunners attract far more volume than long shots. But in this case, the trading patterns deviated sharply from the norm. Just $173,000 was wagered on Ahmed winning, compared to more than $41 million traded on his chief of staff, Shimelis Abdisa, becoming the country’s next leader. Altogether, the volume traded added up to over $285 million, nearly all on losing candidates.

68da8cc8875eed8c: BRUSSELS: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday hailed his first meeting with Hungarian prime minister Peter Magyar as "very good", as Kyiv and Budapest sought a thaw in relations after years of friction.
Since Hungary's pro-EU conservative leader took office in May, both countries have tried to mend ties that were tense under Magyar's Kremlin-friendly predecessor Viktor Orban.
"We've had a very good meeting," Zelensky told reporters in Brussels, where he had spoken with Magyar on the sidelines of an EU summit.
He said that they had discussed "a lot of things, including relations, the economy and logistics - all of which are important between our two countries".
Their meeting comes days after Kyiv passed legislation addressing Budapest's longstanding concerns over the rights of the ethnic Hungarian minority in western Ukraine.
Hungary saw the move as "a first step towards restoring mutual trust", Magyar said on Friday in a statement.
Following the vote, Hungary agreed to allow the EU to open up new areas in accession negotiations with Ukraine.

794076dc1b391155: SINGAPURA: Singapura akan mengeluarkan notis langkah pencegahan di bawah Akta Pencemaran Jerebu Rentas Sempadan (THPA) kepada tujuh syarikat di Indonesia yang disyaki terbabit dalam kebakaran hutan sehingga memburukkan jerebu, kata Menteri Kemampanan dan Alam Sekitar Grace Fu.

d77dc004353cc539: KUALA LUMPUR: The Bar Council has questioned on what basis the Negeri Sembilan state government continues to operate after the appointments of all state executive council members was revoked by the state ruler.

Bar Council president Anand Raj said the matter required clarification, given the revocation of the executive councillors' appointments by the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, amid a dispute over a purported proclamation to remove him.

Anand said the proclamation on April 19, which the Attorney-General's Chambers had rejected as invalid, failed to meet a requirement under the state constitution for a full enquiry by the undangs (traditional territorial chiefs) before they can call upon the ruler to withdraw from his functions or abdicate.

"No contemporaneous record has been published to show that any such enquiry was ever held, nor that His Royal Highness was ever given an opportunity to rebut the allegations made against him,” Anand said in a statement today.

He said the right to be heard was a fundamental principle of natural justice which applied to everyone, including the head of state. Citing a Privy Council decision in a 1962 suit against the Federation of Malaya, he said: “If ordinary citizens are constitutionally protected from unlawful removal from office without a fair hearing, His Royal Highness is entitled to no less protection.”

Anand also said several unanswered questions remained over the handling of the crisis, including the claim by menteri besar Ismail Lasim that he had signed under duress a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz.

“The public is entitled to know by whom, how and why, and why he lodged the police report only on Sept 8, some five weeks after the purported proclamation” and also why the menteri besar subsequently endorsed the proclamation, Anand said.

ac4fce70c466a220: The US' bankruptcy courts are currently down owing to what officials are calling a “cybersecurity incident.” The Administrative Office of the US Courts said the websites and systems that support the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC), which manages electronic comms related to bankruptcy cases, were pulled offline while the vendor investigates. BAE Systems runs the affected systems and websites on behalf of the Federal Judiciary, and is “working to restore operations,” according to an announcement by the US Courts on Thursday. “As a result of the incident, all access to the BNC systems and websites that BAE operates on behalf of the judiciary and the related bankruptcy noticing process are unavailable at this time, including bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov, and the National Creditor Registration Service," it said. “The incident has also halted the BNC’s production and distribution of bankruptcy notices for bankruptcy courts.” While the public notice was published on Thursday, the issues affecting the BNC systems began a few days earlier, on October 9, according to the Bankruptcy Court of the Eastern District of Texas. Alongside its own announcement, the same court published a general order indicating that for any case filed on or after September 14 with an active motion to stay, that delay would be extended by an additional 30 days. The court said it will continue to accept filings, open cases, and process documents, but said there may be a delay in the entry and service of notices and orders until the issues are resolved. The courts' ability to process electronic and paper bankruptcy notices is affected, and it applies to federal bankruptcy courts across the country. A spokesperson at BAE told The Register: "BAE Systems, Inc. operates the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) on behalf of the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AOUSC). We are aware of a security incident that is isolated to the BNC system and have taken immediate steps to address it. We are coordinating closely with AOUSC on the response." The disruption comes at a difficult time for the US public sector, which has struggled with multiple recent cyberattacks. ShinyHunters' attack on the FBI in September is doubtless the most high-profile of these, although the Arizona Judicial Branch confirmed an attack on the state’s court systems at around the same time. Officials said the “criminal hackers or their bots” were responsible for stealing personal data and backup court files. The US Courts also said in August 2025 that it was stepping up its cybersecurity measures in response to increased targeting of its case management system. ®

f41ce474aa96f0d8: SINGAPORE: Seven Indonesian companies are to be sent notices by the Singapore environment agency to put out forest fires that have contributed to worsening air quality caused by smoke pollution from transboundary haze.
The island republic's environment minister, Grace Fu, said the notices would be issued following investigations into errant companies found responsible for causing transboundary haze in Singapore.

"Our investigation so far suggested that some of the haze experienced in Singapore originated from fires on the lands of seven companies in Indonesia. Where warranted, we will take further action under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act based on the information and evidence available," she said at a press conference today.

Fu said the notices seek the companies to deploy firefighting personnel to extinguish fires on land owned or occupied by them and prevent the fires from spreading. They are also required to discontinue or not commence any burning activities and submit action plans detailing measures to extinguish fires on their land and prevent their recurrence.
The minister said the haze conditions in Singapore were expected to persist for some time with air quality likely to fluctuate and potentially reach hazardous levels.

"However, as we transition to the inter-monsoon period towards the end of October or early November, we expect the situation to improve and that is another three to four weeks away. We expect winds around Singapore to become lighter then and more variable in direction, so it is less likely to bring haze from Sumatra or Kalimantan to Singapore," she added.

As of 7pm on Friday, the 24-hour rolling average air pollution index continued to deteriorate with three regions recording very unhealthy air quality at 225 in the central region, 202 in the west, 201 in the east, 183 in the south and 161 in the north.

Fu said the distribution of N95 masks to vulnerable Singaporeans through 37 vending machines will be fully deployed across the island tonight. Sufficient stocks were available at retailers' warehouses and in government stockpiles, she said.
The Asean haze monitoring centre said scattered hotspots were detected in Kalimantan and southern Sumatra, while few isolated hotspots were detected elsewhere.

Moderate to dense smoke haze was observed over parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Kalimantan, Sumatra, and western Sarawak. Moderate to dense smoke haze was also observed over Papua, Sulawesi, the Maluku Islands and the eastern parts of Sabah.
Air quality stations in Singapore and Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy to very unhealthy levels, while air quality stations in Borneo and Sumatra reported unhealthy to hazardous levels.
fcfc778147b16e31: TOKYO, Oct 16 — Napoleon Bonaparte ordered a wartime message written in code, creating a puzzle that remained unsolved for more than 200 years — until artificial intelligence cracked it in a matter of hours.
AI is helping non-specialists unlock the secrets of historical sources, a development described as a “turning point” in a field previously dominated by scholars and dedicated hobbyists.
One new sleuth is Carter Church, a 27-year-old AI engineer who deciphered a 19th-century letter to one of Napoleon’s generals.
Without digital tools, the task could have taken weeks, but the latest model from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI broke the cipher in just six hours.
“What AI mostly brings is persistence,” Church told AFP, saying he felt “an unbelievable sense of satisfaction and excitement when I saw the result”.
The message, dating from 1809, detailed the positions of French and allied troops in two dozen lines of symbols, numbers and letters, but had been left untouched in an online academic archive.

Traditional, low-tech methods of cracking ciphers are effective but time-consuming and labour-intensive, meaning historians “have more important problems to solve, so many ciphers like this often sit unattended”, Church said.
Church, who works at US cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, needed to learn “very little” about code-breaking techniques or the historical period to solve the puzzle.
After spending several evenings working on it, he consulted Japanese patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online list of unsolved ciphers, to verify the solution.

“2026 will be remembered as a turning point for codebreaking of historical ciphers,” Tomokiyo wrote on his website Cryptiana, a go-to resource for the small but enthusiastic global community of amateur cryptographers.
‘Mixed feelings’
Researchers had already been developing AI models to crack ciphers, but the public release of advanced general-purpose tools has unleashed a wave of new solutions.
Although Church used OpenAI’s most powerful model, GPT-6 Astra, others have turned to leading offerings from rival US AI company Anthropic.
Tomokiyo said that since mid-September, AI had been used to crack most of the ciphers on his list.
“There remain some tough problems” that could stay unsolved for years because there is less relevant data available to help AI decipher them, the 58-year-old told AFP.
“I’m excited long-time problems are now solved, but on the other hand, I have mixed feelings, because AI seems to have solved these difficult problems so easily,” he said.
As the technology threatens to take away the satisfaction of being the first to crack a cipher, one fellow code-breaker told Tomokiyo: “I feel useless.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Founder of the Cryptiana website Satoshi Tomokiyo poses for a photo in Tokyo on October 7, 2026; his online database of unsolved ciphers has seen most of its listed codes cracked by AI since mid-September. — AFP pic
AI is surpassing human abilities in fields ranging from mathematics to computer programming, while threatening to transform or even eliminate many jobs.
The technology is also changing historical research beyond code-breaking, helping researchers analyse millions of medieval manuscripts and decipher ancient scrolls.
The Herculaneum Papyri – hundreds of papyrus scrolls carbonised by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 – are too fragile to be unrolled without risking their destruction.
Researchers are now using X-rays and AI to reveal the hidden writing inside them.
In June, researchers in Italy announced the first complete virtual unrolling of a scroll, which turned out to contain a treatise on ethics.
‘Facebook of the past’
AI is also being used to build a vast, searchable collection of previously inaccessible sources on Jewish history and culture by transcribing 10 million pages of Hebrew manuscripts.
“It’s gigantic. No human being could process such a quantity of data,” said project leader Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra of the École Pratique des Hautes Études in Paris.
Researchers hope databases built from the digitised texts – which he likens to a “huge Facebook of the past” – will help uncover connections between people, places and ideas.

At Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, an AI system has been trained to transcribe 14,600 pages of Latin from the church’s medieval archives, a task that also involves deciphering difficult historical writing.

“These are minutes drawn up by notaries who abbreviate their decisions. The script is highly administrative, very pragmatic... with rather technical vocabulary,” said historian Julie Claustre, who leads the e-NDP project.
With character recognition rates ranging from 88 to 94 per cent, the project has revealed information about the cathedral’s daily life, construction work, staff and care of abandoned children.
Doing the same work by hand would take “several decades”, Claustre said, adding that the benefits went beyond saving time.
Automation enables “inquiries that were not previously possible; it transforms the conditions of research”. — AFP
1b86a75417ea40a6: PARIS, Oct 16 — Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have built up a missile and drone arsenal capable of launching varied and sustained strikes, as Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government it backs are finding out.
‘Tit for tat’ strategy
Since early September, the Houthis have struck key oil infrastructure and airports across Saudi Arabia, notably Riyadh’s airport, which has been targeted 20 times.
They have also unsuccessfully targeted the cities of Medina and Mecca.
The trigger for their return to hostilities, after a four-year truce, was a Saudi bombardment of the airport in Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, in July to prevent a Houthi delegation from landing there.
Since then, there have been “tit-for-tat” military strikes, said April Longley Alley, a specialist on Yemen at the Washington Institute think tank.
“The Houthis framed this campaign as blockade for blockade, airport for airport, escalation for escalation,” she said.
Varied arsenal
The Houthis possess a wide range of ballistic missiles and drones, which they are also using to strike targets in the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the entrance to the Red Sea.

The group’s missile stocks partly come from arsenals seized when it took Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, in 2014, as well as “whole systems smuggled in, or self-manufactured systems built from parts that were themselves smuggled into Yemen, primarily via the Arabian Sea”, explained Niranjan BS, a strategic weapons analyst at Jane’s, the open-source intelligence company.

According to the International Institute for Strategic Studies’ Military Balance database, the Houthis have several types of medium-range missiles, some derived from Iranian models such as the Kheibar Shekan.
They also have short-range missiles, including the Asef anti-ship missile, derived from Iran’s Khalij Fars class of missile, noted the Wilson Center think tank.

In addition, the Houthis have a range of cruise missiles from Iran’s Quds missile family, with the Version 4 believed to have a range of 2,000 kilometres (1,200 miles), according to the Wilson Center.
They also have a range of aerial and maritime drones, at least some of which are derived from Iranian models.
The Waeid-1 and Waeid-2 aerial drones, for example, are “local copies of the Iranian Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 one-way attack UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles) respectively”, Niranjan said.
Iran’s support
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Supporters of the Houthi authorities brandish their weapons during a protest against Saudi intervention in Yemen, in Sanaa, on October 9, 2026. — AFP pic
“Iran has provided critical military assistance to the Houthis, particularly with the delivery of missiles and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems,” the Middle East Institute said in a report.
“Missile and UAV parts are designed and manufactured in Iran and smuggled into Yemen via small boats, container ships, or over the Oman-Yemen border, where they are assembled,” it said.

However, Danny Citrinowicz, an Israeli analyst specialising in Iran, cautioned that the Houthis “see themselves as partners of Iran, not proxies. This is why when people are saying Iran instructed the Houthis, it’s not working like that”.
“The Iranians have a strong presence in Yemen,” established by the Quds Force, the foreign operations arm of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, he said at a recent conference in Paris.
But those operatives only advise; they do not decide Houthi operations, he said.

In June 2024, the US Treasury imposed sanctions on a man in China suspected of links to the Houthis, who it said played “a key role in procuring materials that enable Houthi forces to manufacture advanced conventional weapons inside Yemen”.
Able to endure
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The Houthis, who are fighting the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, seized the coastline along a crucial trade route during a lightning offensive last month, extending their control over all of Yemen's Red Sea coast. Yemeni government forces have been attempting for several days to retake coastal territory captured by the pro-Iranian fighters. — AFP pic
Having already weathered years of conflict, the Houthis are seen as capable of using their arsenal for a long time to come.

“We need to remember with the Houthis that they have withstood punishing air campaigns before, from the Saudis, from the Americans, and from the Israelis,” said Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.
“This is a battle-hardened group, and they have much less to lose than the Saudis.”
She added that “the Houthis are probably calculating that they can go longer because they’re used to absorbing these strikes”. — AFP
43f008a3895a3bfe: LONDON, Oct 16 — British filmmaker Mike Leigh said he wished he could make “another hundred films” but fears ill health may prevent him from continuing, as he attended the London premiere of his award-winning latest work on Thursday.

“But it may not be possible, just from a practical point of view.”
Leigh won the top prize at the San Sebastian Film Festival last month for the drama about social workers supporting vulnerable people, which is expected to be his final feature film.
He previously won the top prize at the Cannes Film Festival in 1996 for Secrets and Lies and at the Venice Film Festival in 2004 for Vera Drake.
Actress Alice Bailey Johnson, one of the stars of his latest film, said she was “heartbroken” at the prospect that it could be the socially engaged filmmaker’s final work.
“But if it is, then I can’t express how honoured I feel to be part of it,” she told AFP before the screening.
“It’s just a wonderful moment, and I will treasure it forever.” — AFP
7f93cff45ab1e6a5: MEXICO CITY, Oct 16 — Veronica Rosas is one of tens of thousands of Mexican mothers searching for a child who disappeared into a vortex of violence fuelled by brutal cartel turf wars.
Now, artificial intelligence may offer new hope to families searching for Mexico’s more than 134,000 missing people.
Two new AI tools are being developed to help families and investigators find answers.
Rosas’ son, Diego, was 16 when he went missing in the central town of Ecatepec in September 2015 after leaving home to meet some friends.
The state prosecutor’s office said he was kidnapped by a criminal gang but has not established which group was responsible, why he was taken or whether he is still alive.

“It’s been 11 years and I still don’t know where Diego is. There’s no line of investigation leading us to find out what happened to my son,” Rosas, 52, told AFP at a demonstration in Mexico City, one of many held regularly to demand justice.
Cases like Diego’s have prompted two universities to develop AI tools that they hope will provide answers.
Regresa, meaning “Return”, was developed by Mexico’s main public university, the National Autonomous University of Mexico.

It uses anthropometry – the measurement of the human body – to generate images showing how the faces of missing children may have changed over time, updating images on missing persons posters that otherwise remain frozen at the age they disappeared.
With investigations often dragging on for years, updated likenesses are a recurring demand from families.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

(Left to right) Karla Lechuga, Alejandra Romero, and Ingrid Loana Baca, members of the Lirios Buscadores Izcalli collective, walk in the courtyard of at a church in Tepoztlan, state of Morelos, Mexico, on August 29, 2026 in search of new leads for children who disappeared during the brutal cartel turf war that lasted years. — AFP pic
Countries such as the United States, India and China already use facial recognition and age-progression software to search for kidnapped children.
In Mexico, some prosecutors’ offices use the technology, but most software relies on open-source photo databases that do not reflect typical Mexican features.
Regresa’s developers took a different approach, creating their own image bank using hundreds of photos and data from 75 Mexican volunteers to produce portraits with more typically Mexican features.
Anthropologist Ana Juarez, one of the project’s founders, said Regresa also uses a different technology to age the children’s faces.

“Many software programs only work with facial contours or textures, or add filters that simulate wrinkles. We seek to develop a scientific approach that shows how a person grows in craniofacial terms,” she told AFP, referring to imaging that predicts changes in the skull and face.
Peace boxes and posters
Years of official inaction have driven many families in Mexico to conduct their own investigations into the disappearances of their loved ones.
AI is also being used by an anthropologist at the private Ibero-American University to help make those searches more targeted.
Emiliano Zolla is mapping missing people by gender, age and the circumstances of their disappearance in the hope of helping families narrow their searches.

His observations, based on data about cases in the State of Mexico, the country’s most populous state, include that many of the missing are young women who disappear while travelling to or from school or work.
Rosas said AI could be a game-changer after learning about Regresa from AFP.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A member of the search team walks with a K9 sniffer dog while looking for missing child Brenda Aguilar Guadalupe, in Tepotzotlan, Mexico State on March 13, 2026. — AFP pic
“This initiative is very important because they’re not the little people who were taken back then,” she said.
Rosas has set up a makeshift mailbox bearing a picture of Diego at 16 on Mexico City’s main avenue, inviting people to leave clues about his whereabouts or birthday greetings for him.
Karla Lechuga formed a search collective after her 19-year-old son, Jeshua Cisneros, disappeared in 2025.
Groups like hers have installed dozens of “peace boxes” in churches across the country to gather information about missing people.
They also put up photographs of their missing loved ones in public spaces and urge criminal groups to provide anonymous tips.
“We have found some people alive, unfortunately others not,” Lechuga said.
ba07d6521564176f: Setiap kali isu gaji pekerja dibincangkan di Malaysia, tumpuan hampir selalu tertumpu kepada gaji minimum. Setiap kenaikan kadarnya daripada RM900 sehingga RM1,700 hari ini dan dijangka naik kepada RM1,900 pada tahun hadaman menjadi tajuk utama, topik perbahasan Parlimen, dan penanda aras kejayaan dasar buruh negara.

Persoalan yang jarang ditanya secara terbuka ialah: adakah gaji minimum benar-benar keutamaan paling mendesak bagi pekerja atau adakah kita telah mengabaikan masalah lain yang mungkin mempunyai impak yang lebih besar, iaitu ketiadaan jaminan kenaikan gaji tahunan minimum?
Jawapannya mempunyai implikasi besar ke atas bagaimana dasar buruh negara sepatutnya diutamakan pada masa hadapan.
Siapa sebenarnya dapat manfaat?

Menurut data rasmi Jabatan Perangkaan Malaysia (DOSM), gaji median pekerja sektor formal kini berada dalam lingkungan RM2,900 hingga RM3,200 sebulan, iaitu hampir dua kali ganda kadar gaji minimum RM1,700. Ini bermakna majoriti pekerja, termasuk ramai pekerja perusahaan kecil dan sederhana (PKS), sebenarnya sudah berada di atas paras gaji minimum, dan mungkin kurang mendapat manfaat langsung setiap kali kerajaan mengumumkan kenaikan kadar tersebut.

Bagi kumpulan majoriti ini, satu-satunya laluan untuk gaji mereka meningkat ialah menerusi kenaikan gaji tahunan yang diberi majikan. Namun begitu, seperti yang dinyatakan di bawah Akta Kerja, kenaikan gaji tahunan adalah tidak wajib. Ia bergantung kepada polisi syarikat, dengan kenaikan gaji ditentukan sepenuhnya oleh kontrak kerja, buku panduan pekerja (employee handbook), prestasi kewangan syarikat, serta penilaian prestasi individu. Majikan hanya terikat untuk membayar gaji pokok atau elaun seperti yang dipersetujui dalam kontrak perkhidmatan dan mematuhi undang-undang berkaitan gaji minimum serta tarikh bayaran gaji.

Keadaan ini mewujudkan satu jurang dasar yang kritikal: tumpuan dasar buruh negara selama ini lebih menumpukan kepada golongan paling bawah di dalam rantaian gaji (melalui gaji minimum), namun kurang memberi perhatian kepada kumpulan majoriti pekerja termasuk ramai pekerja PKS yang bergaji sedikit lebih tinggi daripada paras gaji minimum, dan kenaikan gaji mereka bergantung kepada kriteria di atas tanpa sebarang jaminan.

Selain memberi penekanan kepada gaji minimum, dasar buruh negara perlu meneroka mekanisme baharu bagi memperkukuh perlindungan pekerja secara keseluruhan. Antaranya, setiap pekerja tanpa mengira gaji semasa perlu dijamin menerima sekurang-kurangnya satu kadar kenaikan gaji tahunan minimum (contohnya terikat kepada Indeks Harga Pengguna atau kadar tetap seperti 2%–3% setahun).

Mekanisme ini secara tidak langsung akan memberi manfaat lebih besar kepada pekerja dalam sektor teknikal, vokasional dan kemahiran, memandangkan kumpulan ini biasanya tidak mempunyai laluan kerjaya yang formal dan sukar mendaki tangga kerjaya berbanding pekerja dalam laluan profesional atau pengurusan yang sudah mempunyai struktur kenaikan gaji dan pangkat yang lebih jelas.

Pertama, berbanding kenaikan tahunan minimum, gaji minimum, secara definisi, hanya melindungi golongan paling bawah di dalam struktur gaji. Selain itu, kenaikan gaji minimum bagi pekerja baharu akan meningkatkan rasa tidak puas hati kepada pekerja senior dalam organisasi. Kenaikan tahunan minimum pula, jika dilaksanakan, akan melindungi setiap pekerja tanpa mengira paras gaji semasa mereka termasuk pekerja PKS yang gajinya sudah berada di atas RM1,700 tetapi masih jauh daripada gaji sara hidup (living wage) yang munasabah.

Kedua, seperti yang telah dibincangkan, kenaikan gaji minimum yang tidak diikuti oleh kenaikan setimpal untuk pekerja sedia ada mencetuskan mampatan gaji di mana pekerja lama mendapati gaji mereka hampir menyamai pekerja baharu. Justeru, kenaikan tahunan minimum, jika berkuat kuasa untuk semua pekerja secara konsisten setiap tahun, secara struktur akan mengelakkan jurang ini daripada terus mengecil tanpa disedari.

Kenaikan gaji minimum berlaku secara tidak menentu kerana ia bergantung kepada belanjawan tahunan, tekanan politik dan rundingan tiga pihak (kebiasaannya antara kerajaan, majikan dan kesatuan). Pekerja tidak dapat merancang kewangan jangka panjang berdasarkan sesuatu yang tidak menentu masa dan kadarnya. Kenaikan tahunan minimum, sebaliknya, memberi kepastian tahunan yang membolehkan perancangan kewangan lebih baik.

Namun begitu, tidak dapat dinafikan bahawa kenaikan tahunan minimum sekiranya diwartakan akan mendatangkan beberapa cabaran seperti beban kos tahunan kepada majikan, risiko kehilangan pekerjaan terutamanya semasa tempoh kemelesetan ekonomi. Selain itu, jika kadar minimum yang ditetapkan terlalu rendah (contohnya sekadar 1%), ia berisiko mengulangi masalah sedia ada, iaitu kenaikan tahunan hanya menjadi formaliti kosong tanpa kesan bermakna kepada taraf hidup pekerja.
Cadangan masa hadapan

Berdasarkan perbincangan di atas, kerajaan disarankan untuk mengkaji kebolehlaksanaan mekanisme kenaikan gaji tahunan minimum pada kadar yang kecil dan sederhana, contohnya berdasarkan kadar inflasi tahunan Indeks Harga Pengguna bagi memastikan kebajikan pekerja terus terpelihara tanpa memberikan beban kewangan yang berlebihan kepada PKS.

Selain itu, fleksibiliti berdasarkan prestasi kewangan syarikat wajar dipertimbangkan dengan membenarkan PKS yang menghadapi kesukaran kewangan sebenar memohon pengecualian sementara, tertakluk kepada pengesahan dan pemantauan oleh Jabatan Tenaga Kerja.

Mekanisme ini juga boleh digabungkan dengan dasar gaji progresif sedia ada bagi memastikan kenaikan gaji tahunan minimum selari dengan peningkatan produktiviti pekerja dan prestasi syarikat, mewujudkan keseimbangan antara kebajikan pekerja dengan kemampuan majikan.

Akhir sekali, penglibatan kesatuan sekerja dan persatuan PKS melalui sesi perbincangan meja bulat perlu dilaksanakan bagi memastikan sebarang mekanisme baharu dirangka secara telus dan mengambil kira kepentingan semua pihak. Pendekatan rundingan tiga pihak yang melibatkan kerajaan, majikan dan pekerja amat penting bagi menghasilkan dasar yang adil, praktikal dan mampan, berbanding pelaksanaan arahan secara sehala oleh kerajaan.
Siti Noormi Alias ialah pensyarah di Jabatan Pemajuan Profesional dan Pendidikan Lanjutan, Fakulti Pengajian Pendidikan, Universiti Putra Malaysia.

c7e93dbe92adf2ae: WASHINGTON: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia acknowledged on Thursday that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the US, as her credentials face scrutiny.
Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

However, the legal credentials of the press secretary, who pesident Donald Trump appointed last week, were called into question after she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.
The 41-year-old graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law.
In a Fox News interview on Thursday, host Sean Hannity asked Zacharia: "You took the bar exam, but you didn't pass the bar exam, correct?"

In a separate interview with conservative media outlet Real America's Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was "distracted and overwhelmed" by plans to move to China with her husband.
"The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn't need the bar in China," she said.
Foreign nationals cannot sit China's bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.
Hannity later asked Zacharia if she had ever taken the bar exam a second time, to which she said: "I did not".
"I had four kids in six years," she said. "It was never my intent to go into the practice of law,"she added.

Zacharia said on Real America's Voice that "many people in the field" had assured her that she could "label myself a lawyer," given her law degree and experience in business law gained in China, where she worked at a Beijing law firm.
She added that she could "provide legal analysis, not legal advice".
"I was very careful how I executed this," she added.
The Campaign for Accountability, a political ethics organisation, called on Wednesday for the California Bar Association to launch an investigation.
"In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn't puffery; it's a crime," the organisation said in a press release.
Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday with an unusually short press conference, answering questions from only three journalists.
She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative press secretary, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.
a280835cafd4ef1b: The UK's competition watchdog wants to designate Microsoft with strategic market status (SMS) in business software, allowing the regulator it to intervene to level the playing field, and says it is considering other areas for investigation. Regulators around the world are watching to see what the UK decides in this case, with bodies such as the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the European Commission mulling similar actions. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is opening a consultation on whether to tag the Redmond software giant with strategic market status in respect of its portfolio of business software applications. This follows an investigation the regulator started back in May into Microsoft’s software portfolio including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and Teams, plus its security, server and operating systems. The watchdog is also probing whether Microsoft enjoys a position of “substantial and entrenched market power” through the suite of software that could be seen as stifling competition and harming buyer choice. It lays out its proposed decision in a document [PDF] and is inviting comments that must be submitted by November 13. The CMA will make its final decision by February 13, 2027. Bargain spotter The CMA makes it clear the company holds a strong position in each of the five areas it investigated (personal computer operating systems, productivity software suites, security software, server operating systems and relational database management systems), and that customers face barriers when switching providers – limiting their choice and weakening the ability of other software developers to offer rival products. Its proposal document notes Microsoft has been by far the largest provider of business software in the UK for decades. It finds that many customers view Microsoft's portfolio as a unified software environment, forming an end-to-end, integrated stack which makes for easier technical integration between products, with discounted pricing for buying whole bundles of applications together. This makes customers less likely to adopt products from alternative providers that may offer similar or superior functionality, as doing so would duplicate licensing costs for products already in their Microsoft bundle, the CMA says. “Organizations should be able to choose the products that work best for them, switch provider when they want to and combine services from different suppliers. We want to ensure businesses have the freedom to choose how they use Microsoft’s products alongside alternatives,” said CMA chief exec Sarah Cardell. Finding that the criteria for SMS designation are met would not imply or assume wrongdoing on Microsoft’s part, the regulator stresses. A separate document [PDF] spells out the potential interventions that the CMA could make. These include ensuring that Microsoft’s technical design choices do not restrict the ability to use other providers; that commercial arrangements (like bundling) do not limit effective competition; and preventing Microsoft from using its market power in business software to distort competition in adjacent activities, such as cloud services. Rivals back licensing scrutiny Cloud providers previously complained that Microsoft's licensing terms make it more costly for companies to deploy Windows Server instances and services such as SQL Server on non-Microsoft clouds. The proposed SMS designation grew out of the CMA’s investigations into whether the big global players were having a negative impact on the cloud services market in the UK. This largely fizzled out with the watchdog securing undertakings from Microsoft and Amazon Web Services (AWS) that they would work to reduce barriers to switching between clouds and operating multi-cloud deployments. In an update, the CMA says that more can be done to address barriers to switching between cloud providers and using multiple cloud services, and it will continue to work with AWS and Microsoft to address them. It also says it its looking into whether customers can freely choose the best AI tools, and whether alternative AI providers have a level playing field to compete against Copilot. In a statement sent to The Register, Microsoft said it does not share the CMA’s views in its proposed decision on business software solutions. “All our products - including Copilot - are open and interoperable, giving customers the ability to use them alongside competing services and choose solutions that work best for them at attractive prices. We will continue engaging constructively to ensure UK customers and businesses carry on benefiting from robust competition,” a spokesperson told us. However, some pressure groups were quick to signal their approval. The Browser Choice Alliance said it welcomes the CMA’s proposed decision, adding that: “BCA members have long experienced how Microsoft leverages its market power from Windows and productivity software to push users towards its Edge browser, even where they’re trying to use an alternative.” The Open Cloud Coalition, which counts Google as a member, said: “Microsoft’s restrictive software licensing practices distort competition in the cloud, harm choice, and increase costs. This once-in-a-generation opportunity to end these practices can strengthen competition and lower customer costs, if the CMA acts quickly and decisively.” ®

0b41b50427e9cb9a: ARAU, Oct 16 — The Perlis Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recovered RM698,255.55 through forfeitures from 2024 to date.

“According to the annual breakdown, 20 IPs were opened in 2024 involving 27 arrests and 13 charges, with a forfeiture value of RM323,872.55. In 2025, 22 investigation papers were opened, 34 arrests were recorded, and 16 charges were brought to court, with a forfeiture value of RM374,168.

“As for 2026, Perlis MACC opened 23 investigation papers, recorded 23 arrests, and brought eight charges to court, with a forfeiture value of RM215,” he was quoted as saying in a statement issued by Istana Arau today.

“These efforts aim to strengthen the public service delivery system, enhance organisational integrity, and close gaps and opportunities for corruption to occur,” he said.

“Perlis MACC also won the Best KPI Management Award 2025 with an evaluation score of 97.45 per cent, besides securing third place for the Best Financial Management Award 2025.

“These achievements demonstrate the dedication of Perlis MACC in balancing enforcement action with continuous preventive measures to foster an administrative environment of integrity, transparency, and accountability,” he said.
At the farewell ceremony, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra thanked Mohd Nor Adha for his service and commitment in leading Perlis MACC for two years and seven months, from March 1, 2024, until tomorrow.

The Raja Muda expressed hope that the experience Mohd Nor Adha gained in Perlis would help him in his new role and in continuing efforts to strengthen integrity, governance and anti-corruption initiatives. — Bernama
156955d06d74862c: Brave Software has set up a secure space so those using its browser can converse with the company's AI assistant in private. At a time when AI agents like Meta's Muse ask for extensive access to personal information, and AI companies repurpose conversations for training, this amounts to swimming against the tide. Following up on an experiment launched last November to implement a confidential channel for LLM conversations with the help of NEAR AI's trusted execution environment (TEE), the browser maker has connected its Leo AI assistant to Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash under the protection of end-to-end encryption. The result is that Brave users can submit a prompt to Leo that gets encrypted on-device and sent over the network using Oblivious HTTP, a protocol for separating network requests from associated content. Brave's AI Gateway forwards the encrypted query to the TEE without passing along the user's IP address. After Brave verifies the enclave's attestation, the browser encrypts the query using a key bound to the TEE. The TEE decrypts the request, runs it through the AI model, and sends back an encrypted response that gets decrypted by the receiving browser. "In 2014, I argued in 'Trust but Verify' that users shouldn't have to place blind trust in the software they rely on," said Brendan Eich, co-founder and CEO of Brave, in a statement. "They should be able to verify it; this is a user-first principle. AI has raised the stakes, yet too much of it still runs on 'trust me bro' promises, often at the user's expense." NEAR AI's confidential AI pipeline is built with Intel TDX and Nvidia Confidential Compute. It includes end-to-end encryption that keeps Brave from knowing what was asked and NEAR AI from knowing who did the asking during the network hop. Data isolation prevents the prompt or response from being read during processing. Responses are signed in the TEE and there's attestation so users can confirm there's no model bait-and-switch. Leo's GLM 5.3 Flash brain may be isolated in this scenario, but Brave's AI bot can still conduct searches from within the TEE via the Brave Search API's LLM context endpoint. And any searches done this way transit via the TEE rather than the user's browser, which keeps the user's IP address out of the picture. The implementation isn't quite complete: Brave intends to work on moving the verification step into the browser and to publish a log of TEE keys, and to provide enclave attestation for exact model weights loaded into memory, among other things. Brave is not the only company trying to make AI less of a data exposure risk. Apple, AWS, Google, Nvidia, and Microsoft all have some form of private cloud compute infrastructure for AI. Then there's Prem AI, which promises encrypted inference, not to mention providers advertising zero data retention, which isn't as verifiable. One way to ensure privacy while using AI is to run inference on local hardware using an open weight model, assuming the model and the machine running it haven't been compromised. ®
7222a44e4552eb9d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Malaysia is on track to exceed its official full-year gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent after the economy expanded by 5.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, economists said.
The Finance Ministry, in its Economic Outlook 2027 report, raised its 2026 real GDP growth projection to 4.8 to 5.3 per cent, up from 4.0 to 4.5 per cent in Budget 2026.

Prof Dr Yeah Kim Leng, director of the economic studies programme at Sunway University’s Jeffrey Cheah Institute, said third-quarter (Q3) GDP growth of 5.3 per cent affirmed the economy’s resilience despite continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.
“With growth hitting 5.5 per cent in the first three quarters, the economy is on track to exceed the full-year official 4.8-5.3 per cent GDP growth expectation,” he told Bernama.
Yeah said growth moderated slightly from the previous quarter but held up well against a challenging external backdrop marked by geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.

“Encouragingly, the manufacturing sector picked up pace, indicating sustained export demand not only for high-value electronics and optical products but also resource-based chemicals, plastics and rubber products that have higher domestic value added,” he added.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest GDP performance was a positive surprise, with growth potentially exceeding the prevailing forecast of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent.
“At 5.3 per cent, the Malaysian economy is seen to be growing above its trend level of around 4.7 per cent,” he said.
Mohd Afzanizam said foreign investors’ positive appetite for Malaysian investments, coupled with stronger demand for technology-related sectors, had helped sustain economic growth.
Full employment also helped support steady consumer spending as inflation remained fairly contained, he added.

Earlier today, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said in its advance estimates report that the economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in Q3 2026, following growth of 6.0 per cent in the preceding quarter.
For the first three quarters of 2026, the economy grew by 5.5 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.
Domestic demand and E&E to sustain growth

RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) is maintaining its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.4 per cent, with its autoregression and leading economic index models pointing to sustained growth of 5.0 to 5.2 per cent in the second half of the year.
“Robust growth of 5.7 per cent in 1H 2026, together with today’s 5.3 per cent growth reading, which was in line with our in-house expectation, reinforces our constructive outlook.
“Looking ahead, economic activity is expected to remain supported by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electrical and electronics (E&E) exports,” it said in a research note today.
RHB IB said private consumption was expected to remain firm, supported by healthy labour market conditions, continued income growth and civil servant salary adjustments.
“Private investment should also remain resilient, driven by infrastructure projects, ongoing data centre developments and capacity expansion in manufacturing.

“Meanwhile, continued digitalisation, automation and favourable global demand should encourage further investment, particularly in manufacturing and information and communication technology,” it said.

In a separate note, Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd also maintained its full-year growth forecast at 5.3 per cent, although the stronger-than-expected advance estimate pointed to an upside risk to its projection.
It said any revision would depend on September’s data and the full GDP release.

“Domestic demand should increasingly drive growth in the 2H 2026, backed by resilient consumer spending, strong services activity and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital infrastructure.
“Implementation of approved projects, rising household incomes, and a firm labour market add further support,” it said.

Kenanga said manufacturing should remain a key growth driver, supported by sustained E&E demand linked to AI and data centre expansion, although growth could slow as the effects of front-loading fade.
External risks remain, OPR hold expected
Mohd Afzanizam said the Malaysian economy remained fairly resilient despite external shocks, particularly the ongoing war in Iran, which could affect global supply chains and fuel costs.

He said proactive government measures, such as targeted fuel subsidies through MyKad introduced last year, along with Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s efficiencies in procuring fuel supplies beyond the Strait of Hormuz, had allowed the economy to operate almost seamlessly.
RHB IB, however, said geopolitical tensions in West Asia, commodity price volatility and shifting trade policies posed risks to the outlook.
“Prolonged tensions and elevated oil prices could raise production and transportation costs while dampening global demand,” it said.

Separately, CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said the stronger third-quarter results pointed to a modest overshoot of its 5.0 per cent growth forecast for 2026, which would be revised after the full Q3 GDP release in November.
“Stronger external demand remains supportive of the manufacturing outlook, particularly in E&E, where manufacturers have reported longer order books,” it said.

Kids are outsmarting social media bans. That’s not a problem we need to solve.

I don’t remember much about Peppy, my first and only pet cat. What I do vividly remember, though, is the day she went missing. I was 10 years old, and I searched everywhere for her, scouting nearby fields and woods until sunset. I made posters. We never found her. I was devastated.

3ca45a3eee3e1bc7: Capita is set to leave 93,000 pension cases waiting for legally required corrections after its disastrous takeover of the Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS), according to the UK’s largest civil service union. The outsourcing biz took over the scheme in December 2025, offering its 1.7 million members a glitchy online portal and a service that has buckled under demand. Thousands have since had trouble receiving payments and or getting their details updated. In a statement, the PCS union - which has around 170,000 members - said the Cabinet Office had confirmed it would miss the March 2027 deadline for cases arising from the McCloud judgment, which found that changes to public service pension schemes unlawfully discriminated against younger members. The ruling required the government to review and, where necessary, correct pension benefits for the affected period. Around 73,000 retired or deceased members and 20,000 deferred members are still waiting, the union said. The deadline to complete these changes was set for March 2025, but in January this year, the government said it would extend the deadline to March 31, 2027. Capita was due to start the work when it took over the CSPS, but PCS claimed the outsourcer was stuck in the design stage it started in July. PCS general secretary Fran Heathcote said: “These people are waiting for legally required corrections to their pensions, yet Capita has still not begun processing the outstanding cases. I don’t know what more the Government needs to see before it finally says enough is enough.” The Register has asked Capita and the Cabinet Office to comment. Capita won the seven-year, £239 million contract to oversee the CSPS in November 2023, taking over from MyCSP, which ran the scheme on behalf of the Cabinet Office under a £238 million contract that was first agreed in 2012. The Register revealed its troubled launch in December last year. Since then, it has hit the lives of civil servants waiting for their pensions, some of whom have been “left struggling to make ends meet at a pivotable point in their life, causing them significant distress and anxiety,” Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of a parliamentary spending watchdog, said in July. Capita’s original contract award for CSPS details “provision of options and benefits calculations resulting from McCloud judgment”. e9e9a3d52fd23433: OCTOBER 16 — Anyone who has spent time in manufacturing knows that even the best-laid plans can change overnight.
A supplier revises its prices, a shipment arrives late, or a customer changes an order at short notice, leaving the production team to work out how best to keep things moving.
For Malaysian manufacturers, these everyday realities now sit alongside shifting trade policies, geopolitical tensions and changing customer expectations.
It is understandable that business leaders are keeping a close eye on what might happen next.
But there is another question worth asking: how well do we understand what is happening within our own businesses today?
Malaysia’s manufacturing sector generated RM1.97 trillion in sales in 2025, up 4.2 per cent from the previous year, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
With 2.4 million people employed in the sector, there is plenty of reason to be optimistic about its contribution to the economy.
The opportunity now is to build on that foundation by helping manufacturers make confident decisions, even when conditions are less predictable.
The value of knowing where you stand
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A worker operates machinery on a manufacturing production line in Malaysia, where manufacturers face pressure to improve productivity, manage costs and respond to changing market conditions. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
For manufacturers serving overseas markets, developments thousands of kilometres away can have very real consequences on the factory floor.
A change in demand can alter order volumes, higher freight costs can eat into margins, and a delayed component can hold up an entire production run.
Of course, no business can control everything happening around it. What it can do, however, is get a clearer view of how these changes affect its operations.

Take a new customer order, for instance. The revenue might look attractive, but can the factory accommodate it without disrupting existing commitments? Are the necessary materials available, and do the original cost estimates still hold?
These are straightforward questions, yet answering them can be surprisingly difficult when information about inventory, production, purchasing and finances sits in different places.
When teams have a shared, up-to-date picture of the business, these conversations become much easier.
Managers can spot potential constraints earlier, explore alternatives and make decisions based on what is actually happening, rather than what they assume is happening.
That does not remove the uncertainty, but it does give businesses more room to respond thoughtfully.
Busy does not always mean better
One thing worth remembering is that growth and profitability do not always move in tandem.
A factory can be running at full capacity while some jobs deliver thinner margins than expected, or an increase in orders can leave too much cash tied up in inventory.
For business leaders, the question is not simply how to secure more orders, but how to make sure those orders contribute to a healthier business.

Having a clearer view of costs and margins by product, customer or job can help management decide which opportunities make commercial sense, where efficiencies might be found and when pricing arrangements need another look.
Monthly reports remain useful, but business rarely waits for the end of the month.
When costs change or a delivery is delayed, being able to understand the implications promptly can make a meaningful difference to the decisions that follow.
Better decisions start with a shared picture
Production needs to know what can realistically be delivered, purchasing needs to understand supplier availability, and finance needs to see how decisions affect costs and cash flow.
These priorities are connected, yet teams can easily end up working with different versions of the same picture.
When information flows across the business, teams can spend less time reconciling numbers and more time deciding what to do next.
A potential delay becomes a chance to explore alternatives early, while a change in material costs can prompt a timely conversation about pricing.
The value lies not simply in having better information, but in giving people the context to act on it.
Confidence comes from being prepared
For Malaysian manufacturers, opportunities remain to explore new markets, improve productivity and move into higher-value activities.
Making the most of them does not require a perfect forecast, but it does require an honest understanding of what the business can deliver and where it can improve.
Unexpected changes will always be part of manufacturing. What matters is how quickly businesses recognise them, understand their implications and respond.

That hinges on having a clear view of increasingly complex, interconnected operations, so manufacturers can make better decisions, improve productivity and move up the value chain in line with the ambitions of Malaysia’s New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030.
* Ben Lim is the regional sales director for Epicor, South-east Asia.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
84ec2b3b3bf2826e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has urged the operator of Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Miri, Sarawak, to review its rescue and firefighting arrangements after a helicopter crash killed five people, including four Health Ministry personnel, on September 8.

The AAIB recommended that aerodrome operator Malaysia Airports Sdn Bhd (MASB) review rescue and firefighting arrangements across its STOLports to ensure auxiliary personnel were properly trained and equipped, and that firefighting equipment and personal protective equipment (PPE) were properly maintained and serviceable.

The bureau said the recommendation followed findings that Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department (Rela) personnel assigned to auxiliary rescue and firefighting duties had responded to the blaze without appropriate firefighting PPE.

“Some of the available PPE exhibited visible signs of deterioration and damage, which could adversely affect the safety and effectiveness of the emergency response,” the AAIB said in its preliminary report.

The report said 12 dry powder fire extinguishers at the STOLport terminal were used by responders and local villagers in an attempt to put out the flames, but the fire continued to burn for several hours.
All five occupants on board – a 30-year-old Malaysian pilot and four Health Ministry personnel – died from severe burn injuries, according to post-mortem findings cited in the report.

The Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm BO105 S helicopter, registered as 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd under the callsign MEDIC3, was conducting a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight.

The aircraft is designed for various operations, including passenger transport, utility work, medical evacuation and other specialised missions, with a maximum take-off mass of about 2,500kg, depending on its configuration.

The report said a 37-second ground-based video captured the helicopter’s final moments, showing it in flight with a visible smoke trail and apparent flames behind the main gearbox as it approached Runway 04.
The helicopter came to rest about 25 metres from the runway threshold and was destroyed by fire.
All communication frequencies were operating normally, and no emergency call or distress transmission from the helicopter was recorded between departure and the crash, the report said.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department found that weather conditions near Long Lellang STOLport were generally good, with horizontal visibility exceeding 10km during the period assessed.
As an immediate safety measure, Layang-Layang Aerospace suspended operations of aircraft fitted with the same engine type pending airworthiness verification.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia cleared the affected aircraft to return to service on September 13 after technical reviews, the report said.

A detailed examination of the wreckage will be conducted to establish the nature and extent of the damage and, where possible, the sequence and development of the fire and ground-contact damage. The findings will be included in the final report.

The Transport Ministry said information in the preliminary report could be revised as additional evidence emerged, while a comprehensive analysis and the investigation’s conclusions would be presented in the final report.
The ministry said the investigation was intended to prevent similar accidents from recurring, rather than determine fault or liability.

“The ministry appreciates the efforts of the AAIB and the cooperation of all parties involved in assisting the investigation, and remains committed to strengthening the country’s aviation safety,” it said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Rela stands for Jabatan Sukarelawan Malaysia, or the Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department in English.

“The group was led by the woman’s husband, and she invited her friends for a trip to Japan, with each given a pair of shoes that had been pre-stuffed with drugs,” he said.
He said another Malaysian, who was not arrested in connection with the case, was a travel agent and had been cleared of involvement.
Hussein previously said checks confirmed that the group had departed from Terminal 2 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Japanese customs authorities found the drugs inside the shoe soles worn by all the suspects.
He said the NCID had sent a team to Japan to investigate and gather details of the case.
On the drug seizure in Laos, he confirmed that the illicit substances transported on a private jet had been ordered by two Filipino nationals.
He said police were working with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency to track down the individuals and the syndicate involved.
He also said the Royal Malaysia Police were awaiting confirmation on whether the syndicate involved politicians in the Philippines, as reported by the media there.
On October 1, Laotian police seized 521 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine inside a Learjet private aircraft that had arrived from Subang at Luang Prabang International Airport in Laos.

Following the incident, 13 individuals, including Malaysian, Singaporean and Philippine nationals, were detained by Laotian authorities to assist investigations into the transnational drug trafficking case.

404f8ec42e77f4e2: It might not be the Year of the Linux Desktop yet, but it could be the Year of Corporate Compliance on the Linux Desktop as Microsoft releases Defender for Linux Workstations. The product is an extension of Microsoft's existing Defender for Endpoint. According to the Windows behemoth, it brings "enterprise-grade protection, detection, vulnerability management and response capabilities to Linux workstations." Linux desktop users will get services including Defender's anti-virus functionality. The penguin-primed product also has management tools for inventory and security settings, as well as device isolation. "The result," said Microsoft, "is broader Linux protection, delivered through the tools and processes security teams already trust." The release is currently in public preview and requires the standalone Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5 and E7. Support is based on the underlying Linux distribution and kernel version, with RHEL, CentOS, Ubuntu LTS, SUSE Linux Enterprise Server, and Oracle Linux among others on the list. There's no separate desktop agent to deploy or maintain. Defender works the same way as it does on Linux servers, so administrators shouldn't face many challenges. End users… well… that's another story. As enterprises gain visibility into Linux workstations alongside the rest of their endpoint estate, some friction is possible and it won't be technical. For some, compliance through Microsoft's tooling is anathema, no matter how penguin-friendly it claims to be nowadays. As for the why, we're told it's simple business and customer demand. Microsoft noted that more developers are using Linux desktops, which in turn makes them more attractive to attackers. "As Linux adoption expands beyond the datacenter, organizations need a consistent approach to protecting Linux wherever it is used," Microsoft said. The idea of Microsoft Defender being able to peer at Linux desktops may alarm some, but Microsoft announced Defender ATP for Linux back in 2020. The better question is: why has it taken so long? We'd also quibble with the premise "As more developers begin to use Linux desktops." Many already do: the 2025 Stack Overflow survey had Windows leading for professional work at 49.5 percent, but Ubuntu wasn't far behind at 27.7 percent. So less "begin," more "enthusiastically continue." ®
0745649d7e523d9e: WASHINGTON, Oct 16 — New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia acknowledged today that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States, as her credentials face scrutiny.
Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

But the legal credentials of the press secretary, who President Donald Trump appointed last week, were called into question after she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.
The 41-year-old graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law.
In a Fox News interview on Thursday, host Sean Hannity asked Zacharia: “You took the bar exam, but you didn’t pass the bar exam, correct?”

In a separate interview with conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move to China with her husband.
“The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn’t need the bar in China,” she said.
Foreign nationals cannot sit China’s bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.
Hannity later asked Zacharia if she had ever taken the bar exam a second time, to which she said: “I did not.”
“I had four kids in six years,” she said. “It was never my intent to go into the practice of law.”

Zacharia said on Real America’s Voice that “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer,” given her law degree and experience in business law gained in China, where she worked at a Beijing law firm.
She added that she could “provide legal analysis, not legal advice.”
“I was very careful how I executed this.”
The Campaign for Accountability, a political ethics organization, called on Wednesday for the California Bar Association to launch an investigation.
“In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime,” the organization said in a press release.
Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday with an unusually short press conference, answering questions from only three journalists.
She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative press secretary, who stepped down in August to care for her young children. — AFP
dbb80731d80a6390: PARIS, Oct 16 — After weeks of student protests, France is set to be swept by broader, nationwide demonstrations Saturday over the cost of living, setting up a potentially fraught period ahead of presidential elections next year.

The prospect of the two movements merging, perhaps with outbreaks of violence, poses a big challenge to the government — and an opportunity for far-left and far-right presidential candidates jockeying for power.

The country’s Yellow Vest movement, which eight years ago staged street protests against President Emmanuel Macron and his government, called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations and urged millions to turn out.
It has appealed to teachers, workers, pensioners and farmers, as well as students, in an online call spread through social media.
“I have a feeling that (Saturday) will be a sort of culmination,” 18-year-old Marie-Lou, a protesting university student in the city of Lille, told AFP.
“We’ll be joined by workers and by the Yellow Vests, who are also mobilising again. There’s a sense of hope that all these different struggles might converge.”
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Thursday he feared clashes after what he called “urban violence” during the student protests.
Lecornu is under pressure to get a cost-cutting budget through parliament. It aims to tackle France’s growing public debt by raising more tax revenue and reducing expenditures.
Yet the Yellow Vest and student movements are demanding the government spend more money.
They want protection from inflation sent surging above three percent by the Middle East war, and boosted public services, particularly education.
Anger at police
There is also public anger at perceived police brutality during the student protests, during which several teenage protesters were maimed and thousands were arrested.

Francois Boulo, a figure within the Yellow Vest movement, told AFP there was no coordination with the various groups expected to take part Saturday, “but we all had the same reaction when we saw the police violence against the students”.

The growing unrest on France’s streets and the country’s fragmented political system are weighing on the final months of Macron’s presidency, ahead of elections in April and May to choose his successor.
They are also fertile ground for opposition parties and their candidates.
Jean-Luc Melenchon, leader of the far-left France Unbowed party, has backed the student protests and marched in a demonstration Tuesday supporting them.
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner according to surveys, has positioned her National Rally party on the side of the police, consistent with its law-and-order messaging.
Macron this week said he believed the “legitimate” demands of the protesting students were being “exploited for political purposes”, according to a government spokeswoman.
Prepared for violence
Organisers of tomorrow’s demonstrations have set up a website showing more than 500 demonstrations planned across France.
The Paris police banned a major march through the tourist and business heart of the capital, saying it could only take place in the east of the city.
But authorities and demonstrators were both preparing for possible violence.
Paris police have launched legal action against an influencer on Twitch who urged his hundreds of thousands of followers to take part in the demonstration “war zone”.

And on Friday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told France 2 television that officers could use stun grenades in case of “extremely serious urban violence”. He had previously suspended their use during the student protests after one stun grenade blew off the hand of a 15-year-old.
Demonstrators have set up a smartphone app giving the real-time location of police, tear gas and helicopters. — AFP
